docs.title: proxy_start
docs.text:
Start a proxy listener with optional configuration. The proxy listens on the specified address and begins intercepting HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS5 traffic. You can run multiple listeners simultaneously by assigning each a unique name.

Reset semantics -- not a delta-apply tool

Each proxy_start call fully resets all prior session settings to the values supplied in the request. Fields omitted from the request revert to their defaults -- including capture_scope, tls_passthrough, intercept_rules, auto_transform, tcp_forwards, SOCKS5 auth, TLS fingerprint, and connection/timeout limits. Use proxy_start for first-time startup or session initialization. For in-session partial updates to a running listener (adding a single rule, changing one timeout, etc.), use configure instead.

See Common misuse: proxy_start as a partial-update tool below for the anti-pattern and the recommended initialize-then-configure workflow.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description name string No "default" Listener name for multi-listener support listen_addr string No "127.0.0.1:8080" TCP address to listen on (loopback only) upstream_proxy string | object No direct Upstream proxy URL (http://host:port or socks5://host:port), or a rotation object. See upstream_proxy capture_scope object No capture all Controls which requests are recorded tls_passthrough string[] No [] Domain patterns that bypass TLS interception intercept_rules array No [] Rules for intercepting requests/responses auto_transform array No [] Rules for automatic request/response modification tcp_forwards object No {} TCP forwarding map (port -> target string or ForwardConfig object) socks5_auth string No "none" SOCKS5 authentication method (none or password) socks5_username string No Username for SOCKS5 password auth socks5_password string No Password for SOCKS5 password auth tls_fingerprint string No "firefox" TLS ClientHello fingerprint profile client_cert string No PEM client certificate path for mTLS client_key string No PEM client private key path for mTLS max_connections integer No 512 Maximum concurrent connections (1--100000) max_concurrent_streams integer No 500 HTTP/2 SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS advertised to clients (1--65535) peek_timeout_ms integer No 30000 Protocol detection timeout in ms (100--600000) request_timeout_ms integer No 60000 Request-head timeout in ms: HTTP/1.x request line + headers, CONNECT request, client TLS handshake (100--600000)

docs.title: upstream_proxy
docs.text:
Routes all outgoing traffic for this listener through an upstream proxy. It takes precedence over the HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY environment variables. Two shapes are accepted.

String form -- a literal proxy URL. http://host:port uses HTTP CONNECT, and socks5://host:port uses SOCKS5. Add credentials with http://user:pass@host:port (Basic) or socks5://user:pass@host:port.

Object form -- enables per-listener rotation for the live MITM data path:

Field Type Description url string Literal proxy URL (same as the string form). Mutually exclusive with url_template url_template string Proxy URL template using §var§ syntax. §__nonce§ expands to a fresh UUID per resolution event, and §__iteration§ to an index rotation.policy string Required with url_template: per_request, per_connection, per_target_host, or sticky Policy When the template is re-expanded per_request Every outbound TCP dial. For HTTP/2, the dial is the rotation event, not each stream per_connection Once per inbound client connection; all upstream dials from that client share the URL per_target_host Once per target host (cached with a TTL); different hosts get different URLs sticky Once for the listener's lifetime. Calling configure or proxy_start again clears it

The template is probe-expanded when you call the tool, so a malformed template, a disallowed scheme, or CRLF in the expanded URL fails the call instead of the first live dial. Each listener owns its own resolver, so rotation state never leaks between listeners. The query status resource reports the active rotation per listener in listeners[] as upstream_proxy_template (credentials redacted) and upstream_proxy_rotation_policy.

docs.title: capture_scope
docs.text:
Controls which requests are recorded to the flow store.

  • includes (array of scope rules) -- only matching requests are captured. If empty, all requests match.
  • excludes (array of scope rules) -- matching requests are excluded. Takes precedence over includes.

Each scope rule has:

Field Type Description hostname string Hostname pattern (exact or *.example.com wildcard) url_prefix string URL path prefix (e.g. "/api/"), compared byte-exact against the wire-form path (percent-encoding not decoded, query excluded) method string HTTP method (e.g. "GET", "POST")

At least one field must be set per rule.

docs.title: intercept_rules
docs.text:
Each intercept rule has:

Field Type Required Description id string Yes Unique rule identifier enabled boolean Yes Whether the rule is active direction string Yes "request", "response", or "both" conditions object Yes Matching criteria (AND logic)

Conditions:

Field Type Description host_pattern string Regex for hostname matching (port excluded) path_pattern string Regex for URL path matching. Matched against the wire-form path (percent-encoding not decoded, query string excluded) on HTTP/1.x and HTTP/2 methods string[] HTTP method whitelist (case-insensitive) header_match object Maps header names to regex patterns (AND logic)

Multiple rules use OR logic -- a request/response is intercepted if any enabled rule matches.

docs.title: tcp_forwards
docs.text:
Maps local listen ports to upstream forwarding configurations. Each entry maps a port number (string key) to either a string or a ForwardConfig object.

String format (legacy) -- the value is an upstream host:port address. Traffic is relayed as raw bytes with no L7 parsing:

"3306": "db.example.com:3306"

ForwardConfig object format -- provides control over protocol detection and TLS termination:

Field Type Required Default Description target string Yes -- Upstream address in host:port format protocol string No "auto" Expected protocol for L7 parsing tls boolean No false Enable client-side TLS MITM termination on the forwarded listen port upstream_tls boolean No false Wrap the upstream-dial connection in TLS (USK-911 / USK-916). Independent of tls -- target's scheme/port are advisory only upstream_insecure_skip_verify boolean No inherit -insecure Per-entry override for upstream TLS certificate verification when upstream_tls=true. Set true to skip verification on this entry, false to enforce, or omit to inherit the global Config.InsecureSkipVerify (USK-918)

Protocol values:

Value Description "auto" Peek-based detection -- the proxy inspects initial bytes to determine the L7 protocol "raw" No L7 parsing -- relay as opaque bytes (same behavior as the legacy string format) "http" Parse traffic as HTTP/1.x "http2" Parse traffic as HTTP/2 "grpc" Parse traffic as gRPC (over HTTP/2) "websocket" Operator-declared expectation that the request initiates an RFC 6455 Upgrade "sse" Operator-declared expectation that the upstream returns a text/event-stream response (USK-913)

Server-speaks-first protocols

For targets where the server sends first (SMTP, FTP, MySQL, IMAP, POP3), use "raw". With "auto", the proxy waits up to 5 seconds for the client's first bytes before falling back to raw, which delays the server's greeting.

TLS modes (tls × upstream_tls matrix):

tls and upstream_tls are independent: tls controls the client-direction handshake on the listen port; upstream_tls controls the upstream-direction handshake to target. The four combinations cover the realistic deployment shapes:

tls upstream_tls Client wire Upstream wire Typical use case false false plaintext plaintext Raw L4/L7 forwarding (default) true false TLS plaintext TLS termination only (downstream offload) false true plaintext TLS Plaintext client -> TLS-only upstream true true TLS TLS Full MITM: terminate then re-encrypt upstream

When tls=true, the proxy issues a certificate using the target hostname and applies L7 parsing to the decrypted traffic. When upstream_tls=true, the proxy uses the global TLS fingerprint, SNI derived from target, and the configured verification / client-cert settings -- or the per-entry upstream_insecure_skip_verify override.

Note

Setting tls: true with protocol: "raw" is valid but unusual -- TLS is terminated, yet the decrypted payload is relayed as raw bytes without L7 parsing.

Both formats can be mixed in the same tcp_forwards object.

Port collision with listen_addr

Any tcp_forwards port that matches the listen_addr port is rejected fail-fast before binding (port 0 on either side is exempt because the kernel assigns distinct ephemeral ports). The check protects against silently-broken listeners that would otherwise be registered but fail to bind.

docs.title: tls_fingerprint
docs.text:
Value Description "firefox" Mimic Firefox browser TLS fingerprint (default) "chrome" Mimic Chrome browser TLS fingerprint "safari" Mimic Safari browser TLS fingerprint "edge" Mimic Edge browser TLS fingerprint "random" Random browser fingerprint per connection "none" Standard Go crypto/tls (no fingerprint mimicry)

With "firefox" (the default), the upstream HTTP/2 send-shape -- SETTINGS values and order, the connection-level WINDOW_UPDATE, and pseudo-header order -- is also shaped like Firefox, so the TLS and HTTP/2 fingerprints stay coherent. Both are pinned to Firefox 120, the newest profile the TLS library provides. Other profiles keep the default HTTP/2 send-shape. See TLS configuration.

docs.title: Connection limits and timeouts
docs.text:
• max_connections -- connections refused at the cap are reported in the query status resource under connection_rejections, and recorded as flows with blocked_by: "capacity".
  • request_timeout_ms -- covers each HTTP/1.x request line and header section (measured from the request's first byte, on every keep-alive request), the CONNECT request, and the client-side TLS MITM handshake. The request body is not covered. A client that misses the deadline is disconnected without a response; for an HTTP/1.x request head, the event is recorded as an error flow with failure_reason: "request_head_timeout". Idle client keep-alive connections are closed after 120 seconds (or request_timeout_ms, if longer).

docs.title: Response
docs.text: Field Type Description name string Listener name listen_addr string Actual address the proxy is listening on status string Proxy state ("running") tcp_forwards object Configured TCP forwarding map (if any)

docs.title: Common misuse: proxy_start as a partial-update tool
docs.text: proxy_start is not a delta-apply tool. Calling it repeatedly to "add one more intercept rule" wipes every other setting that was previously established for the listener.

docs.title: Anti-pattern (do NOT do this)
docs.text:
// proxy_start -- step 1: set up the session
{
  "listen_addr": "127.0.0.1:8080",
  "capture_scope": {"includes": [{"hostname": "api.target.com"}]},
  "tls_passthrough": ["*.googleapis.com"]
}

// proxy_start -- step 2 (WRONG): trying to add an intercept rule.
// This RESETS capture_scope back to "capture all" and clears tls_passthrough,
// because both fields are omitted from this second request.
{
  "listen_addr": "127.0.0.1:8080",
  "intercept_rules": [
    {
      "id": "r1",
      "enabled": true,
      "direction": "request",
      "conditions": {"host_pattern": "api\\.target\\.com"}
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Recommended pattern: initialize with proxy_start, update with configure
docs.text:
// proxy_start -- one-shot initialization
{
  "listen_addr": "127.0.0.1:8080",
  "capture_scope": {"includes": [{"hostname": "api.target.com"}]},
  "tls_passthrough": ["*.googleapis.com"]
}

// configure -- in-session update: add an intercept rule without touching the rest
{
  "operation": "merge",
  "intercept_rules": {
    "add": [
      {
        "id": "r1",
        "enabled": true,
        "direction": "request",
        "conditions": {"host_pattern": "api\\.target\\.com"}
      }
    ]
  }
}

See configure for the full merge / replace surface (add, remove, enable, disable per rule ID, or full-section replacement).

docs.title: Start with defaults
docs.text:
// proxy_start
{}

docs.title: Start on a custom port
docs.text:
// proxy_start
{
  "listen_addr": "127.0.0.1:9090"
}

docs.title: Start with capture scope and TLS passthrough
docs.text:
// proxy_start
{
  "listen_addr": "127.0.0.1:8080",
  "capture_scope": {
    "includes": [
      {"hostname": "api.target.com"},
      {"hostname": "*.target.com", "url_prefix": "/api/"}
    ],
    "excludes": [
      {"hostname": "static.target.com"}
    ]
  },
  "tls_passthrough": ["*.googleapis.com", "accounts.google.com"]
}

docs.title: Start with intercept rules
docs.text:
// proxy_start
{
  "intercept_rules": [
    {
      "id": "target-host",
      "enabled": true,
      "direction": "request",
      "conditions": {
        "host_pattern": "httpbin\\.org"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "admin-api",
      "enabled": true,
      "direction": "request",
      "conditions": {
        "host_pattern": "api\\.target\\.com",
        "path_pattern": "/api/admin.*",
        "methods": ["POST", "PUT", "DELETE"],
        "header_match": {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Start with TCP forwarding (string format)
docs.text:
// proxy_start
{
  "listen_addr": "127.0.0.1:8080",
  "tcp_forwards": {
    "3306": "db.example.com:3306",
    "6379": "redis.example.com:6379"
  }
}

docs.title: Start with TCP forwarding (ForwardConfig with protocol detection)
docs.text:
// proxy_start
{
  "listen_addr": "127.0.0.1:8080",
  "tcp_forwards": {
    "50051": {
      "target": "api.example.com:50051",
      "protocol": "grpc"
    },
    "8443": {
      "target": "secure.example.com:443",
      "protocol": "http2",
      "tls": true
    },
    "3306": "db.example.com:3306"
  }
}

docs.title: TCP forward with upstream TLS and per-entry verification override
docs.text:
// proxy_start
{
  "listen_addr": "127.0.0.1:8080",
  "tcp_forwards": {
    "50051": {
      "target": "grpcbin.local:50051",
      "protocol": "grpc",
      "upstream_tls": true,
      "upstream_insecure_skip_verify": true
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Start with a rotating upstream proxy
docs.text:
// proxy_start
{
  "listen_addr": "127.0.0.1:8080",
  "upstream_proxy": {
    "url_template": "http://session-§__nonce§:pass@residential.example:8080",
    "rotation": {"policy": "per_target_host"}
  }
}

docs.title: Start with SOCKS5 password authentication
docs.text:
// proxy_start
{
  "listen_addr": "127.0.0.1:8080",
  "socks5_auth": "password",
  "socks5_username": "proxyuser",
  "socks5_password": "proxypass"
}

docs.title: Start multiple listeners
docs.text:
// proxy_start
{
  "name": "http-listener",
  "listen_addr": "127.0.0.1:8080"
}

// proxy_start
{
  "name": "socks-listener",
  "listen_addr": "127.0.0.1:1080"
}

docs.title: Start with TLS fingerprint
docs.text:
// proxy_start
{
  "listen_addr": "127.0.0.1:8080",
  "tls_fingerprint": "firefox"
}

docs.title: proxy_stop
docs.text: Stop proxy listener(s). Performs a graceful shutdown, waiting for existing connections to complete before stopping.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description name string No Listener name to stop. If omitted, all running listeners are stopped

docs.title: Response

docs.title: Stop all listeners
docs.text:

{}

docs.title: Stop a specific listener
docs.text:
// proxy_stop
{
  "name": "http-listener"
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The proxy must be running; otherwise an error is returned.
  • Active connections are allowed to finish before the server shuts down.
  • After stopping, you can call proxy_start again to restart.
  • Intercept holds still pending when the listener stops end without an intercept action and are recorded with blocked_by: "intercept_cancelled" (see query).

docs.title: query
docs.text: Unified information query tool. Retrieve flows, flow details, messages, proxy status, configuration, CA certificate, intercept queue, macros, fuzz jobs, and fuzz results.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description resource string Yes Resource to query (see below) id string Conditional Flow ID or macro name. Required for flow, messages, and macro fuzz_id string Conditional Fuzz job ID. Required for fuzz_results filter object No Filter options (see below) fields string[] No all Fields to include in the response sort_by string No Field to sort results by limit integer No 50 Maximum items to return (max 1000) offset integer No 0 Items to skip for pagination include_bodies boolean No true Include message bodies in responses. When false, body fields are suppressed; metadata, headers, and body_truncated remain. Mirrors manage.export_flows.include_bodies body_max_bytes integer No 0 Truncate per-message body to at most this many bytes (0 = no cap). When applied, body_truncated_by_query=true and body_original_size reports the pre-truncation length decode_bodies boolean No true Decode HTTP Content-Encoding (gzip / deflate / br / zstd) into *_body_decoded fields. The original wire-form body is always returned in *_body. Set false to skip decoding for performance

docs.title: filter
docs.text: Field Type Applies to Description protocol string flows Canonical Message-type family. One of "http", "ws", "grpc", "grpc-web", "sse", "raw", "tls-handshake". See Protocol family filter scheme string flows Wire-observed handshake transport: "http", "https", "tcp". Use scheme=https to match all TLS flows regardless of HTTP version. Application-level schemes (ws, wss) are rejected -- combine protocol="ws" with scheme="https" for WS-over-TLS http_version string flows HTTP version filter: "http/1.0", "http/1.1", "h2", "h2c". Empty-string explicit value matches pre-USK-788 rows that lack a recorded version origin string flows Stream origin filter: "proxy" (live capture), "resend" (resend_* tools), "fuzz" (fuzz campaigns) method string flows HTTP method filter (e.g. "GET", "POST") url_pattern string flows URL substring match status_code integer flows, fuzz_results HTTP status code filter blocked_by string flows Blocked flow filter: "target_scope", "intercept_drop", "intercept_cancelled", "rate_limit", "safety_filter", "budget", or "capacity". See Blocked flows state string flows Flow lifecycle state ("active", "complete", "error") conn_id string flows Connection ID filter (exact match) host string flows Host filter (matches server_addr or request URL host) wire_level string flows, messages Wire-fidelity overlay selector: "semantic" (default; the canonical application-level envelope), "h1-chunk", "h2-frame", "grpc-lpm-frame", "grpcweb-base64", or "all". Overlay rows are hidden from message_count / message_preview and from default messages listings unless this filter explicitly includes them. See Wire-level overlays below direction string messages Message direction ("send" or "receive") body_contains string fuzz_results Response body substring filter outliers_only boolean fuzz_results Return only outlier results status string fuzz_jobs Job status filter (e.g. "running", "completed") tag string fuzz_jobs Job tag filter (exact match)

docs.title: Protocol family filter
docs.text:
The filter.protocol value matches a canonical Envelope.Protocol family. Each canonical value expands across every wire spelling the proxy may have recorded for that family:

Value Matches http HTTP/1.x and HTTP/2 traffic, including TLS variants and SOCKS5-tunnelled spellings ws Native WebSocket and SOCKS5-tunnelled WebSocket grpc Native gRPC over HTTP/2 grpc-web gRPC-Web (HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 transports) sse Server-Sent Events raw TCP-passthrough and Raw flows tls-handshake TLS handshake records observed without a higher-level decode

Only these canonical values are accepted -- the legacy literals (HTTP/1.x, HTTPS, HTTP/2, WebSocket, gRPC, gRPC-Web, TCP, SOCKS5+...) were retired in N9. Use filter.scheme to find all TLS flows (e.g. scheme=https returns HTTP/1.x + HTTP/2 + gRPC over TLS).

docs.title: Wire-level overlays
docs.text:
A single application-level (semantic) flow may be persisted alongside one or more wire-level overlay rows that capture the exact wire bytes at a lower protocol layer. These overlays are forensic detail: they let you inspect the wire even when the semantic envelope has been re-encoded or reassembled.

wire_level value Records semantic (default) The canonical application-level envelope (HTTPMessage, GRPCDataMessage, WSMessage, SSEMessage, ...) h1-chunk One row per HTTP/1.x chunked-transfer chunk boundary h2-frame One row per HTTP/2 DATA frame (per direction, per stream), including WS/SSE-over-h2 paths grpc-lpm-frame One row per gRPC length-prefixed-message frame grpcweb-base64 One row per gRPC-Web base64-encoded body chunk all Include every wire-level row alongside semantic

Overlay rows are excluded by default from flow.message_count, flow.message_preview, and messages listings. Pass filter.wire_level="h2-frame" (etc.) to surface them, or wire_level="all" to get every layer.

HAR export ignores the wire_level filter -- HAR is a semantic format. Use the JSONL export (manage.export_flows with filter.wire_level) when forensic preservation of the wire matters.

docs.title: gRPC schema-aware decode
docs.text: When grpc_schema has a registered descriptor for the flow's (grpc_service, grpc_method) pair and decode_bodies=true, the body is decoded via protojson with real .proto field names and body_decoded_encoding="proto-json" is set on the response. On parse failure the proxy falls back to the schemaless path and surfaces body_decode_anomaly { type: "proto_schema_mismatch" }. Without a registered schema, gRPC bodies fall back to schemaless decode (body_decoded_encoding="proto-schemaless-json").

docs.title: HTTPMessage anomalies
docs.text: Parser-detected anomalies on HTTP messages (header smuggling indicators, malformed framing, etc.) are persisted on the flow row and surfaced by the flow and messages resources under anomalies[]. Filter for flows that carry an anomaly by combining protocol=http with a body-level filter, or fetch the full flow detail for inspection.

docs.title: flows
docs.text:
List recorded proxy flows with optional filtering and pagination.

Each flow entry includes a protocol_summary field with protocol-specific information:

  • WebSocket: message_count, last_frame_type
  • HTTP/2: stream_count, scheme
  • gRPC: service, method, grpc_status, grpc_status_name
  • TCP: send_bytes, receive_bytes

Returns: flows[], count, total.

docs.title: flow
docs.text:
Get full details of a single flow including request/response headers, bodies, and connection info. Requires id.

Flow state values:

  • "active" -- in progress (send recorded, awaiting receive)
  • "complete" -- finished successfully
  • "error" -- failed (e.g. 502 error, upstream connection failure)

For streaming flows (flow_type != "unary"), the response includes message_preview (first 10 messages) and message_count. Use the messages resource with limit/offset to page through all messages.

When intercept/transform modifies a request, the original_request field contains the pre-modification request data, including a body_truncated flag.

For TLS connections, conn_info carries the client's ClientHello fingerprints as tls_client_ja3 and tls_client_ja4, alongside tls_version, tls_cipher, tls_alpn, and tls_server_cert_subject.

The url field (in flow, flows[], messages[], and original_request) carries the request path in wire form -- percent-encoding exactly as sent, not decoded. Because a JSON string cannot carry invalid UTF-8, any such path or query bytes are shown %XX-escaped with upper-case hex (the wire byte 0xFF appears as %FF); every other byte is verbatim. resend_http with flow_id still replays the original wire bytes, not the escaped text.

docs.title: Request heads closed by the proxy
docs.text:
HTTP/1.x request heads the proxy closed before the request was complete are recorded as "error" flows with tags.closed_by = "proxy" and one of these failure_reason values:

failure_reason Meaning request_head_timeout The request line and headers did not arrive within request_timeout_ms (tags.request_timeout_ms holds the value in force). An idle keep-alive connection with zero bytes of a next request is not recorded request_line_too_long The request line exceeded the parser limit; the proxy answered 414 URI Too Long request_header_too_large The header section exceeded the parser limit; the proxy answered 431 Request Header Fields Too Large

tags.phase is request_line or headers. raw_request holds the bytes received, capped at max_raw_capture_size (metadata.raw_truncated = "true" marks a capped capture, and metadata.raw_captured_bytes gives its length). For 414 / 431, the proxy-generated response is in response_status_code / raw_response (message metadata.proxy_generated = "true"); tags.wrote_response = "false" means the response could not be written. These flows share conn_id with earlier requests on the same connection. Because a client can create them by sending a partial or oversized request head, capture_scope and max_raw_capture_size bound what is stored.

docs.title: Blocked flows
docs.text:
blocked_by Meaning target_scope Blocked by the target scope policy intercept_drop Dropped by an intercept drop action intercept_cancelled An intercept hold that ended without an intercept action because the connection or proxy went away while it was held (proxy_stop, session teardown, the peer direction failing). State is error, and the stream id equals the held entry's stream_id rate_limit Rejected by a rate limit safety_filter Blocked by the Safety Filter budget Rejected because the diagnostic budget was exhausted capacity The proxy refused the connection because max_connections was reached. State is error, server_addr is the refused target (CONNECT authority, HTTP/1.x absolute-form authority, or TCP forward target), and tags.target is the request target as received. Written at most about 10 per second and only for targets inside capture_scope; the full count is in status -> connection_rejections

Like other blocked flows, no flow rows carry the held or rejected content.

docs.title: messages
docs.text:
Get paginated messages within a flow. Requires id. Supports limit, offset, and filter.direction.

Returns: messages[], count, total.

  • body_encoding: "text" for UTF-8 safe bodies, "base64" for binary content.
  • metadata: Protocol-specific fields (e.g. WebSocket opcode, gRPC service/method/grpc_status).

docs.title: status
docs.text:
Get current proxy status and health metrics. No additional parameters.

Returns: running, listen_addr, listeners[], listener_count, upstream_proxy, active_connections, max_connections, peek_timeout_ms, request_timeout_ms, total_flows, db_size_bytes, uptime_seconds, ca_initialized, socks5_enabled, tls_fingerprint, rate_limits, budget, h1_upstream, h2_upstream, connection_rejections, export_dir.

Field Description listeners[] Per-listener name, listen_addr, active_connections, uptime_seconds, upstream_proxy, and -- while upstream proxy rotation is active -- upstream_proxy_template (credentials redacted) and upstream_proxy_rotation_policy h1_upstream HTTP/1.x upstream redial / replay counters: stale_detected_healthcheck, write_epipe, redial_healthcheck, redial_write_epipe, redial_failed_healthcheck, redial_failed_write_epipe, replay_success, ... h2_upstream HTTP/2 upstream redial counters: goaway_observed_prewarm, goaway_observed_reactive, refused, redial_prewarm, redial_reactive, redial_refused_stream, prewarm_suppressed, and the matching redial_failed_* counters connection_rejections Connections refused because max_connections was reached, counted since server start: total, last_at, by_kind (http1, connect, socks5, http2, tcp, unknown), recent[] (newest first: at, listener, forward_port, remote_addr, detected_kind, method, target, target_truncated, wrote_503, max_connections, recorded), unrecorded (audit flows shed by the write-rate cap or a full recorder queue), and out_of_scope (not recorded because capture_scope excludes the target) export_dir Directory that manage export_flows / import_flows file paths are confined to. Empty means file export / import is disabled

Modified intercept variants surface as separate flows

When an intercept rule modifies a request or response, both the original and the modified envelope are recorded as separate flows. The modified flow receives a fresh UUID id (no longer the legacy -modified suffix) and carries metadata.variant = "modified" so import round-trips stay consistent. Filter on variant=original|modified (or read the metadata field) to distinguish them.

docs.title: config
docs.text:
Get the current configuration. No additional parameters.

Returns: upstream_proxy, tls_passthrough (patterns, count), tcp_forwards, socks5_enabled, client_cert, safety_filter (enabled, input_rules, output_rules), max_connections, peek_timeout_ms, request_timeout_ms, tls_fingerprint, size limits (max_raw_capture_size, max_body_size, body_spill_threshold, ...), capture_scope (includes, excludes), intercept_queue, and export_dir.

intercept_queue echoes the current hold-queue settings in the same shape that configure returns (timeout_ms, timeout_behavior, queued_items, per-protocol overrides). It is omitted until the proxy has started.

docs.title: ca_cert
docs.text:
Get the CA certificate PEM, metadata, and persistence state. No additional parameters.

Returns: pem, fingerprint, subject, not_after, persisted, cert_path, install_hint.

docs.title: intercept_queue
docs.text:
List intercepted requests/responses currently waiting in the intercept queue. Supports limit.

Each item includes a phase field: "request" (pre-send) or "response" (post-receive).

Returns: items[], count.

docs.title: macros
docs.text:
List all stored macro definitions with summary information. No additional parameters.

Returns: macros[] (name, description, step_count, created_at, updated_at), count.

docs.title: macro
docs.text:
Get full details of a single macro definition. Requires id (macro name).

Returns: name, description, steps[], initial_vars, timeout_ms, created_at, updated_at.

docs.title: fuzz_jobs
docs.text:
List fuzz jobs with optional filtering. Supports filter.status, filter.tag, fields, limit, offset.

Returns: jobs[], count, total.

docs.title: fuzz_results
docs.text:
Get results for a specific fuzz job with filtering, sorting, and aggregate statistics. Requires fuzz_id.

The summary includes:

  • total_results: Total matching results.
  • statistics: Aggregate stats with status_code_distribution, body_length and timing_ms distributions (min, max, median, stddev).
  • outliers: Result IDs that deviate from baseline (by_status_code, by_body_length, by_timing).

Supports filter.status_code, filter.body_contains, filter.outliers_only, fields, sort_by, limit, offset.

sort_by values: index_num (default), status_code, duration_ms, response_length.

Returns: results[], count, total, summary.

docs.title: resend_grpc
docs.text: Resend a gRPC RPC via a freshly dialled HTTP/2 upstream connection with GRPCStartMessage / GRPCDataMessage / GRPCEndMessage-typed schema. Each call dials a fresh TCP (and TLS for https) connection and opens one HTTP/2 stream.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description flow_id string No Recorded gRPC stream id. When set, omitted Start fields and the encoding hint are inherited from the original RPC target_addr string Conditional Upstream host:port. Required when flow_id is empty. When supplied with flow_id, redirects the dial target while preserving the recovered :authority. Without it, the dial follows the recorded, client-declared :authority -- see What decides the dial scheme string No "https" "http" or "https". http selects plaintext h2c. With flow_id, the recorded :scheme is used, except that a recovered http is dialed over TLS when the proxy observed a TLS upstream for that stream. An explicit "http" always forces cleartext service string Conditional gRPC service name (e.g. "pkg.Greeter"). Required when flow_id is empty method string Conditional gRPC method name (e.g. "SayHello"). Required when flow_id is empty metadata array No Ordered metadata list as [{"name": "...", "value": "..."}]. Preserves wire case, order, and duplicates encoding string No grpc-encoding for outgoing messages ("identity" or "gzip") accept_encoding string[] No grpc-accept-encoding list (e.g. ["gzip", "identity"]) messages array Yes Request-side LPM list (see below). At least one element required trailer_metadata array No Optional Send-direction trailer HEADERS. When supplied, the request terminates via a trailer frame instead of END_STREAM on the last DATA timeout_ms integer No 30000 Per-call timeout in milliseconds tls_fingerprint string No Informational v1; per-call selection is deferred tag string No Tag stored on the new stream's Tags map

docs.title: messages
docs.text:
Each entry is one length-prefixed message (LPM) on the gRPC stream:

Field Type Required Default Description payload string Yes LPM payload interpreted per body_encoding body_encoding string No "text" "text", "base64", "proto-json", or "proto-schemaless-json" compressed boolean No false Set the LPM compression flag. Requires encoding to be set

docs.title: Body encodings
docs.text:
• "text" / "base64" -- send the literal bytes after decoding the text/base64 wrapper. Use these when you have the wire payload in hand.
  • "proto-json" -- the payload is JSON keyed by the registered .proto's field names. The proxy parses it against the schema bound to (service, method) via grpc_schema, encodes it to proto wire bytes, and LPM-frames it. protojson.UnmarshalOptions{DiscardUnknown:true} silently drops keys outside the schema; type mismatches still fail. Without a registered schema this returns a hard error.
  • "proto-schemaless-json" -- synthetic-key JSON via internal/encoding/protobuf. Lossless for unknown fields and extensions, at the cost of opaque numeric keys.

When flow_id is supplied and the source flow carries fields outside the registered schema, the response includes a non-fatal warnings[] entry. See Lossy round-trip on the grpc_schema page for the full mechanics.

docs.title: End semantics
docs.text:
• When trailer_metadata is omitted (the common case): the final messages LPM carries END_STREAM=true and the request terminates via END_STREAM on the last DATA frame.
  • When trailer_metadata is supplied: the trailing DATA keeps END_STREAM=false and a Send-direction trailer HEADERS frame is sent afterwards (a non-standard but diagnostic-useful client-side trailer).

docs.title: What decides the dial with flow_id
docs.text:
A gRPC stream's recorded :authority and :scheme are copied verbatim from the client's HEADERS block, so both are client-declared and untrusted. In flow_id mode:

  • Address -- without target_addr, the dial goes to the recorded :authority. Pass target_addr to pin the destination when the recorded client may have been hostile. Every such call reports this in warnings[].
  • Transport -- a recovered scheme=http is reconciled against the TLS state the proxy observed on the upstream leg. When TLS was observed, the resend dials with TLS anyway and reports it in warnings[], so a spoofed :scheme: http cannot replay recorded authorization metadata in cleartext. An unobserved TLS state never downgrades a recovered https.
  • Wire fidelity -- the resent HEADERS frame still carries the recorded :scheme; only the TCP/TLS handshake differs.
  • Overrides win -- an explicit scheme is always honored.

tcp_forwards false positive

With a tcp_forwards entry that has a plaintext client leg and upstream_tls: true, the recorded :authority is the plaintext forward listener while the observed TLS belongs to the upstream beyond it. Pass "scheme": "http" for that topology.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Field Type Description stream_id string New stream record id holding the resend's send and receive flows start_metadata array Ordered receive-direction GRPCStart metadata [{"name": "...", "value": "..."}] messages array Decoded response-side LPMs (see below) end object Optional trailer summary (see below). May be null when the upstream terminated without a trailer HEADERS frame duration_ms integer Total duration in milliseconds tag string Echo of the supplied tag (when set) warnings string[] Optional non-fatal advisories. Dial-provenance and observed-transport TLS-upgrade notices come first, followed by proto-json unknown-field notices

Each messages[] entry:

Field Type Description payload string Decompressed LPM payload payload_encoding string "text" or "base64" compressed boolean true when the LPM had its compression bit set on the wire

end object:

Field Type Description status integer gRPC status code (0 = OK) message string gRPC status message (when non-empty) trailers array Other trailer fields. Excludes grpc-status, grpc-message, and grpc-status-details-bin

docs.title: Pipeline placement
docs.text:
Each Start and Data envelope traverses PluginStepPost -> RecordStep. End is observation-only (RFC-001 §9.3 surface table marks (grpc, on_end) = PhaseSupportNone).

The resent stream is finalised on completion: Stream.State transitions to "complete" on success or "error" on failure (USK-789). The new flow records origin = "resend".

docs.title: Replay a recorded RPC
docs.text:
// resend_grpc
{
  "flow_id": "grpc-abc-123",
  "messages": [
    {"payload": "{\"name\":\"world\"}"}
  ]
}

docs.title: Construct a new RPC against an h2c target
docs.text:
// resend_grpc
{
  "target_addr": "127.0.0.1:50051",
  "scheme": "http",
  "service": "pkg.Greeter",
  "method": "SayHello",
  "metadata": [
    {"name": "authorization", "value": "Bearer token"}
  ],
  "messages": [
    {"payload": "AAAAAAk=", "body_encoding": "base64"}
  ]
}

docs.title: resend_http
docs.text: Resend or construct an HTTP/1.x or HTTP/2 request with HTTPMessage-typed schema fields. Each call records a fresh stream containing the resend's send and receive flows.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description flow_id string No Recorded stream id. When set, omitted fields are inherited from the original send method string Conditional HTTP method (e.g. "GET", "POST"). Required when flow_id is empty scheme string Conditional "http" or "https". Required when flow_id is empty authority string Conditional Host / :authority value. Sent as :authority over HTTP/2; over HTTP/1.1 it is the default Host header when none is supplied. Required when flow_id is empty path string Conditional Request path including the leading slash. Required when flow_id is empty. A literal ? in path is auto-split into path (before ?) plus raw_query (after ?); supplying both raw_query AND a ? in path returns an error. The path is sent and recorded exactly as given (wire form): percent-encoding is neither decoded nor added. When inherited from flow_id, the recorded wire-form path is replayed byte-for-byte raw_query string No Raw query string without the leading ? headers array No Ordered header list as [{"name": "...", "value": "..."}]. Preserves wire case, order, and duplicates body string No Request body interpreted per body_encoding body_encoding string No "text" "text" or "base64" body_set boolean No false Set true to override the body to empty; otherwise omitting body inherits the original body_patches array No Patches applied on top of any body replacement (see below) override_host string No Redirect the dial target while preserving the request's Host/:authority (must be host:port) follow_redirects boolean No false Unsupported. Setting true returns an error http_version string No recorded flow's, else "http/1.1" Wire protocol for the upstream send: "http/1.1", "h2" (scheme https only, ALPN h2), or "h2c" (scheme http only, prior knowledge). See Wire protocol upstream_proxy object No Per-call upstream proxy override: {"url_template": "..."}. See Upstream proxy override timeout_ms integer No 30000 Per-request timeout in milliseconds tls_fingerprint string No Informational v1; per-call selection is deferred. The server uses its configured fingerprint tag string No Tag stored on the new flow's Tags map

docs.title: body_patches
docs.text:
Each patch is one of:

  • JSON path patch: {"json_path": "$.key", "value": "new"}
  • Regex patch: {"regex": "pattern", "replace": "replacement"}

An optional "encoding" array applies codec transformations as a pipeline.

docs.title: Header validation
docs.text: Header names and values are rejected if they contain CR/LF characters (CWE-113 guard). The list is replaced wholesale when supplied; otherwise the recorded send's headers are inherited.

docs.title: Wire protocol (HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2)
docs.text:
The resend goes out over the protocol the original flow used -- it is never silently downgraded:

Source of the decision Result http_version supplied That protocol (http/1.1, h2, or h2c) flow_id whose recorded http_version is h2 / h2c HTTP/2: h2 (TLS, ALPN) when the resolved scheme is https, h2c (cleartext, prior knowledge) when it is http Anything else (HTTP/1.x flow, unversioned flow, from-scratch request) http/1.1
  • h2 offers the configured ALPN list unchanged, so the ClientHello matches the live proxy path, and requires the upstream to select h2. If it selects anything else, the call fails with an error naming the negotiated ALPN -- pass "http_version": "http/1.1" to downgrade deliberately. HTTP/2 SETTINGS and pseudo-header order follow the configured tls_fingerprint.
  • HTTP/2 headers -- the request target is sent as :method / :scheme / :authority / :path. No Host header is added. Header names are lowercased on the wire and connection-specific headers (Connection, Keep-Alive, Transfer-Encoding, Upgrade, Proxy-Connection, TE other than trailers) are stripped -- relevant when you force an HTTP/1.x flow to h2.
  • HTTP/1.1 pins ALPN to http/1.1 and adds a Host header from authority when the header list has none.
  • The new flows record the protocol actually used in http_version. 1xx interim responses are recorded as their own receive flows; the result fields describe the final response.
  • WebSocket over HTTP/2 (RFC 8441) is not covered -- use resend_ws.

docs.title: Upstream proxy override
docs.text: upstream_proxy.url_template routes this one resend through an upstream proxy (http:// via CONNECT, or socks5://), for example to switch residential proxy IPs. The template uses §var§ syntax and is expanded once per call with the reserved variables §__iteration§ (always 0 for resend) and §__nonce§ (a fresh UUID). The expanded URL is checked for CRLF injection.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: Field Type Description stream_id string New stream record id holding the resend's send + receive flows status_code integer HTTP response status code headers array Ordered response header list [{"name": "...", "value": "..."}] body string Response body (subject to SafetyFilter output masking) body_encoding string "text" or "base64" duration_ms integer Round-trip duration in milliseconds tag string Echo of the supplied tag (when set)

docs.title: Pipeline placement
docs.text:
The resend traverses PluginStepPost -> RecordStep. PluginStepPre and InterceptStep are bypassed (RFC-001 §9.3) so post-mutation hooks fire exactly once on the resent envelope while pre-pipeline annotation hooks stay quiet.

The resent stream is finalised on completion: Stream.State transitions to "complete" on success or "error" on failure (USK-789). The new flow records origin = "resend" so query callers can filter live capture out of analyses via filter.origin = "proxy".

docs.title: Resend with method override
docs.text:
// resend_http
{
  "flow_id": "abc-123",
  "method": "PUT",
  "headers": [
    {"name": "Content-Type", "value": "application/json"}
  ]
}

docs.title: Construct from scratch
docs.text:
// resend_http
{
  "method": "POST",
  "scheme": "https",
  "authority": "api.example.com",
  "path": "/v1/login",
  "headers": [
    {"name": "Content-Type", "value": "application/json"}
  ],
  "body": "{\"user\":\"alice\"}"
}

docs.title: Redirect to a different upstream
docs.text:
// resend_http
{
  "flow_id": "abc-123",
  "override_host": "10.0.0.5:8443"
}

docs.title: Resend through a rotating residential proxy
docs.text:

{
  "flow_id": "abc-123",
  "upstream_proxy": {
    "url_template": "http://user-session-§__nonce§:password@residential.example:8080"
  }
}

{
  "flow_id": "abc-123",
  "http_version": "http/1.1"
}

docs.title: resend_raw
docs.text:
Resend a recorded raw byte payload via a freshly dialled TCP (or TLS) upstream connection. This is the smuggling-and-anomaly-test surface: payload bytes (override_bytes, patches[].data, recovered Flow.RawBytes) are NEVER normalized. They reach the wire verbatim.

flow_id is required -- resend_raw has no from-scratch path. Use fuzz_raw for ad-hoc byte injection.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description flow_id string Yes Recorded raw stream id target_addr string Yes Upstream host:port. Explicit decimal port required (no defaulting -- raw is protocol-agnostic). An empty host (:80), empty port (host:), or service-name port (host:http) is rejected so the target scope check always sees the real port use_tls boolean No false true to upgrade the dialled connection to TLS sni string No target host SNI server name. Defaults to target_addr host portion when use_tls=true override_bytes string No Replacement payload interpreted per override_bytes_encoding. Mutually exclusive with patches override_bytes_encoding string No "text" "text" or "base64". Use "base64" for binary smuggling payloads override_bytes_set boolean No false Set true to replace with empty bytes; otherwise an empty override_bytes string is treated as no override patches array No Offset-based byte patches applied to the recovered bytes (see below). Mutually exclusive with override_bytes insecure_skip_verify boolean No false Skip TLS server certificate verification when use_tls=true tls_fingerprint string No Informational v1; per-call selection is deferred timeout_ms integer No 30000 Per-call timeout in milliseconds tag string No Tag stored on the new flow's Tags map

docs.title: patches
docs.text:
Each entry overwrites bytes at a given offset in the recovered payload:

Field Type Required Default Description offset integer Yes Zero-based byte offset in the recovered payload data string Yes Replacement bytes interpreted per data_encoding (must not be empty) data_encoding string No "text" "text" or "base64"

CR/LF in target_addr and sni is rejected, but never in override_bytes, data, or recovered Flow.RawBytes -- those are the wire and must reach it verbatim.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: Field Type Description stream_id string New stream record id holding the resend's send Flow plus every received chunk Flow response_bytes string Concatenated payload across all received bytechunk envelopes (always base64) response_size integer Total response size in bytes response_chunks integer Envelope count for callers that want the segmentation shape truncated boolean true when the receive loop hit the per-call response cap before the upstream closed duration_ms integer Total duration in milliseconds tag string Echo of the supplied tag (when set)

docs.title: Pipeline placement
docs.text:
The resend traverses PluginStepPost -> RecordStep. PluginStepPre and InterceptStep are bypassed (RFC-001 §9.3).

The resent stream is finalised on completion: Stream.State transitions to "complete" on success or "error" on failure (USK-789). The new flow records origin = "resend".

docs.title: Replay a recorded TCP flow as-is
docs.text:
// resend_raw
{
  "flow_id": "raw-abc-123",
  "target_addr": "10.0.0.5:3306"
}

docs.title: Replay over TLS
docs.text:
// resend_raw
{
  "flow_id": "raw-abc-123",
  "target_addr": "secure.example.com:8443",
  "use_tls": true
}

docs.title: Override the entire payload
docs.text:
// resend_raw
{
  "flow_id": "raw-abc-123",
  "target_addr": "target.example.com:80",
  "override_bytes": "R0VUIC8gSFRUUC8xLjENCkhvc3Q6IGV4YW1wbGUuY29tDQoNCg==",
  "override_bytes_encoding": "base64"
}

docs.title: Apply byte-level patches
docs.text:
// resend_raw
{
  "flow_id": "raw-abc-123",
  "target_addr": "target.example.com:80",
  "patches": [
    {"offset": 0, "data": "POST", "data_encoding": "text"}
  ]
}

docs.title: resend_ws
docs.text: Resend a single WebSocket frame via a freshly dialled upstream connection with WSMessage-typed schema fields. Each call performs a fresh TCP (and TLS for wss) dial, an HTTP/1.1 Upgrade dance, then sends one frame and records the response.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Default Description flow_id string No Recorded WebSocket stream id. When set, the upgrade dance inherits URL, request headers, and the negotiated permessage-deflate extension target_addr string Conditional Upstream host:port. Overrides the dial target while preserving the recovered :authority. Required when flow_id is empty scheme string Conditional "ws" "ws" or "wss". Required when flow_id is empty. Any other value (e.g. "https") is rejected, including alongside flow_id. For target scope, ws matches as http and wss as https path string Conditional Upgrade request path. Required when flow_id is empty raw_query string No Upgrade request raw query string without the leading ? opcode string Yes Frame opcode: "text", "binary", "close", "ping", "pong" fin boolean No true FIN bit payload string No Frame payload interpreted per body_encoding body_encoding string No "text" "text" or "base64" payload_set boolean No false Set true to send an empty payload; otherwise an empty payload field is treated as no override masked boolean No Informational. The upstream-facing layer auto-masks per RFC 6455 §5.3 regardless of this value mask string No Informational 4-byte mask key (base64). Ignored on Send for client-to-server frames close_code integer No RFC 6455 status code for Close frames close_reason string No Optional UTF-8 reason for Close frames compressed boolean No Per-message-deflate (RFC 7692). Requires the upgrade to negotiate deflate via flow_id timeout_ms integer No 30000 Per-call timeout in milliseconds covering dial + upgrade + send + receive tls_fingerprint string No Informational v1; per-call selection is deferred tag string No Tag stored on the new flow's Tags map

CR/LF in path, raw_query, scheme, or target_addr is rejected to prevent request smuggling on the upgrade leg.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Field Type Description stream_id string New stream record id holding the resend's send Flow plus every received frame opcode string Opcode of the upstream's terminating frame (first non-control frame or Close) fin boolean FIN bit on the result frame payload string Result frame payload interpreted per payload_encoding payload_encoding string "text" or "base64" compressed boolean true when the result frame used per-message-deflate close_code integer RFC 6455 status code (Close frames only) close_reason string Close reason text (Close frames only) duration_ms integer Total duration in milliseconds tag string Echo of the supplied tag (when set)

Auto-Pong replies for incoming Pings are emitted by the receive loop and recorded as their own flows on the same stream.

docs.title: Pipeline placement
docs.text:
The resend traverses PluginStepPost -> RecordStep. PluginStepPre and InterceptStep are bypassed (RFC-001 §9.3).

The resent stream is finalised on completion: Stream.State transitions to "complete" on success or "error" on failure (USK-789). The new flow records origin = "resend" so callers can filter live capture out of analyses via query filter.origin.

docs.title: Send a text frame to a recorded stream
docs.text:
// resend_ws
{
  "flow_id": "ws-abc-123",
  "opcode": "text",
  "payload": "{\"action\":\"ping\"}"
}

docs.title: Send a binary frame from scratch
docs.text:
// resend_ws
{
  "target_addr": "ws.example.com:443",
  "scheme": "wss",
  "path": "/socket",
  "opcode": "binary",
  "payload": "AAECAw==",
  "body_encoding": "base64"
}

docs.title: Send a Close frame
docs.text:
// resend_ws
{
  "flow_id": "ws-abc-123",
  "opcode": "close",
  "close_code": 1000,
  "close_reason": "bye"
}

docs.title: security
docs.text: Configure runtime security settings including target scope rules, rate limits, diagnostic budgets, and SafetyFilter inspection. This tool is separate from configure to allow MCP clients to apply different approval policies for security changes.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description action string Yes Action to perform (see below) params object No Action-specific parameters

docs.title: Two-layer architecture
docs.text:
Target scope, rate limits, and budgets use a two-layer architecture:

  • Policy Layer (immutable by the agent) -- set at startup from -target-policy-file, or else the config file's target_scope_policy section. Defines the upper boundary. No MCP tool can modify it; only the operator can replace it at runtime with a SIGHUP reload. Policy rules are validated at startup with the same rules as this tool (except that a policy rule may omit hostname), and an invalid policy stops the server instead of loading a rule that silently matches nothing.
  • Agent Layer (mutable) -- controlled by this tool. Can further restrict access within Policy Layer boundaries.

docs.title: Evaluation order (target scope)
docs.text:
1. Policy denies -- always block (highest priority)
  2. Agent denies -- block
  3. Policy allows (if any) -- target must match at least one
  4. Agent allows (if any) -- target must match at least one
  5. All checks passed -- allow

When neither layer has rules, all targets are permitted (open mode).

docs.title: Where target scope applies
docs.text:
A single shared evaluator applies both layers to all traffic:

Traffic source Deny symptom HTTPS via CONNECT tunnel The proxy returns 200 Connection Established, then closes the connection; the client's inner TLS handshake fails with EOF Plain-HTTP forward proxy 403 Forbidden with body yorishiro-proxy: target blocked by scope MCP tool requests (resend_*, fuzz_*, macro) MCP error response with the violation reason. Fuzz jobs re-check scope for every variant they send Intercept release (release, modify_and_forward, timeout auto-release) The intercept call succeeds, but scope is checked again at release time against the request actually forwarded (for modify_and_forward, the modified one). An HTTP request gets 403 Forbidden with body {"error":"blocked by target_scope","blocked_by":"target_scope"}, a WebSocket / gRPC message is dropped, and the block is recorded as a flow with blocked_by: target_scope

After set_target_scope, update_target_scope, or a policy reload, live connections that an identical new connection would no longer be admitted for are closed. A connection with held intercepts is revoked at once (new requests get 403) but closed only after its holds resolve. A deny that only names a path_prefix closes no connection; it is enforced per request.

docs.title: Reloading the Policy Layer (operator only)
docs.text:
The operator can replace the running Policy Layer -- target scope allows / denies, rate_limits, and budget together -- by editing the policy source and sending the server process SIGHUP (Unix only). There is deliberately no MCP action for this.

  • Enabled only with a policy source -- the handler is installed only when the server was started with -target-policy-file or -config. Without either, SIGHUP terminates the process as before. Wait for the Info log line target scope policy reload enabled before signaling.
  • Terminal hangup -- closing the launching terminal also sends SIGHUP, which now triggers a reload instead of stopping the server. Stop it explicitly with SIGTERM or SIGINT.
  • Full, atomic replacement -- the new source is validated completely before anything changes. A section omitted from the new file is cleared. On any validation error, the previous policy stays in force and target scope policy reload rejected; previous policy retained is logged.
  • Prefer -target-policy-file for live edits -- it is decoded strictly, so a misspelled field rejects the reload. The -config source is decoded leniently, so a typo can reload as "no policy"; a Warn line reports when a reload drops every allow and deny rule.
  • Agent Layer -- agent rules are kept unchanged. An agent allow rule the new policy no longer covers simply stops matching, so narrowing the policy never widens what the agent can reach.
  • Budget -- the request counter is not reset; the duration limit is re-armed against the new value from the original session start.
  • Audit -- a successful reload logs target scope policy reloaded with the source path, file sha256, and rule counts. get_target_scope reports source and loaded_at.

Protect the policy file

Keep the policy file in a directory that neither the proxy's user nor the agent can write, and never where manage export can write.

docs.title: set_target_scope
docs.text: Replace all Agent Layer allow/deny rules. Use empty arrays to clear rules. Agent allow rules must fall within the Policy allow boundary.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description allows array Allow rules denies array Deny rules

docs.title: update_target_scope
docs.text: Apply incremental changes to Agent Layer rules.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Description add_allows array Allow rules to add remove_allows array Allow rules to remove add_denies array Deny rules to add remove_denies array Deny rules to remove

Warning

remove_denies cannot remove Policy deny rules. Attempting to do so returns an error.

docs.title: get_target_scope
docs.text: Returns both Policy and Agent Layer rules with enforcement mode. No parameters.

docs.title: test_target
docs.text: Check a URL against current rules without making a request (dry run).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description url string Yes URL to test

docs.title: set_rate_limits
docs.text: Set Agent Layer rate limits. Omitted fields reset to 0 (no limit). Full-replace semantics.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description max_requests_per_second number Global rate limit in RPS (0 = no limit) max_requests_per_host_per_second number Per-host rate limit in RPS (0 = no limit)

docs.title: get_rate_limits
docs.text: Returns Policy and Agent Layer rate limits with effective values. No parameters.

docs.title: set_budget
docs.text: Set Agent Layer diagnostic budget limits. Omitted fields reset to 0 (no limit). Full-replace semantics.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description max_total_requests integer Max total requests for the session (0 = no limit) max_duration string Max session duration, e.g. "30m" ("0s" = no limit)

docs.title: get_budget
docs.text: Returns Policy and Agent Layer budgets with effective values and current usage. No parameters.

docs.title: get_safety_filter
docs.text:
Returns the current SafetyFilter configuration and rules (read-only). SafetyFilter rules are part of the Policy Layer and cannot be modified at runtime. No parameters.

When the Input Filter blocks a native gRPC call, the RPC fails with grpc-status: 7 (PERMISSION_DENIED) and grpc-message: blocked by safety_filter; the matched rule IDs travel comma-separated in the x-yorishiro-matched-rules trailer. A blocked message in a bidi or client stream ends the whole RPC. gRPC-Web messages are dropped without a status.

docs.title: Target rule fields
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description hostname string Yes Exact match or wildcard *.example.com. IPv4 and IPv6 literals are accepted; IPv6 may be bare (::1) or bracketed ([::1]), and every zone-less form of one address is the same host. A wildcard over an IP literal is rejected ports integer[] No Match specific ports. Empty = all ports path_prefix string No Literal, case-sensitive prefix of the request path (not a glob). Must start with /; *, ?, and # are rejected. Matches when either the wire-form path or its percent-decoded form starts with the prefix (/admin also matches /%61dmin). Empty = all paths schemes string[] No Transport confidentiality: http = plaintext, https = TLS. No other value is accepted. Empty = both. See What schemes means

All specified fields must match for a rule to apply (AND logic).

docs.title: What schemes means
docs.text:
schemes is a transport confidentiality axis, not an application-protocol axis. It applies to every protocol the proxy scopes:

  • A WebSocket target matches as http (ws://) or https (wss://). "schemes": ["ws"] is rejected.
  • A raw TCP or gRPC target matches as https when the leg is TLS-terminated, and http when it is cleartext.
  • A CONNECT tunnel matches as https, even if it turns out to carry another protocol.
  • SOCKS5 targets are scope-checked before the tunnel carries any byte, so no schemes-bearing rule matches them. Scope them by hostname / ports.

A schemes condition narrows a rule in both directions: a deny rule with "schemes": ["https"] does not block the plaintext dial to the same host, and an allow rule with "schemes": ["https"] does not permit one. Omit schemes when you mean "this host, on any transport" -- the safer default for deny rules.

docs.title: set_target_scope / update_target_scope
docs.text: Field Type Description status string "updated" allows array Current Agent Layer allow rules denies array Current Agent Layer deny rules mode string "open" or "enforcing"

docs.title: get_target_scope
docs.text: Field Type Description policy object Policy Layer: allows, denies, source, loaded_at, immutable agent object Agent Layer: allows, denies effective_mode string "open" or "enforcing"

docs.title: test_target
docs.text: Field Type Description allowed boolean Whether the URL is allowed reason string Reason for the decision layer string Which layer decided ("policy" or "agent") matched_rule object The rule that matched (if any) tested_target object Parsed URL components: hostname, port, scheme, path

docs.title: set_rate_limits
docs.text: Field Type Description status string "updated" effective object Merged Policy+Agent limits agent object Current Agent Layer values

docs.title: get_rate_limits
docs.text: Field Type Description policy object Policy Layer limits agent object Agent Layer limits effective object Merged effective limits

docs.title: set_budget
docs.text: Field Type Description status string "updated" effective object Merged Policy+Agent limits agent object Current Agent Layer values

docs.title: get_budget
docs.text: Field Type Description policy object Policy Layer budget agent object Agent Layer budget effective object Merged effective budget request_count integer Requests made so far stop_reason string Non-empty when budget is exhausted

docs.title: get_safety_filter
docs.text: Field Type Description enabled boolean Whether SafetyFilter is active input_rules array Input filter rules (block destructive payloads) output_rules array Output filter rules (mask PII) immutable boolean Always true -- rules cannot be changed at runtime

docs.title: Set target scope
docs.text:
// security
{
  "action": "set_target_scope",
  "params": {
    "allows": [
      {"hostname": "api.target.com", "ports": [443], "schemes": ["https"]},
      {"hostname": "*.target.com"}
    ],
    "denies": [
      {"hostname": "admin.target.com"}
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: Update target scope incrementally
docs.text:
// security
{
  "action": "update_target_scope",
  "params": {
    "add_allows": [{"hostname": "new-api.target.com"}],
    "remove_allows": [{"hostname": "old-api.target.com"}],
    "add_denies": [{"hostname": "staging.target.com"}]
  }
}

docs.title: Test a URL against scope rules
docs.text:
// security
{
  "action": "test_target",
  "params": {
    "url": "https://api.target.com/v1/users"
  }
}

docs.title: Get current target scope
docs.text:
// security
{
  "action": "get_target_scope"
}

docs.title: Set rate limits
docs.text:
// security
{
  "action": "set_rate_limits",
  "params": {
    "max_requests_per_second": 10,
    "max_requests_per_host_per_second": 5
  }
}

docs.title: Set diagnostic budget
docs.text:
// security
{
  "action": "set_budget",
  "params": {
    "max_total_requests": 1000,
    "max_duration": "30m"
  }
}

docs.title: Get current budget
docs.text:
// security
{
  "action": "get_budget"
}

docs.title: Get SafetyFilter configuration
docs.text:
// security
{
  "action": "get_safety_filter"
}

Example response:

{
  "enabled": true,
  "input_rules": [
    {
      "id": "destructive-sql:drop",
      "name": "DROP statement",
      "pattern": "(compiled regex)",
      "targets": ["body", "url", "query"],
      "action": "block",
      "category": "destructive-sql"
    }
  ],
  "output_rules": [
    {
      "id": "credit-card:separated",
      "name": "Credit card (separated)",
      "pattern": "(compiled regex)",
      "targets": ["body"],
      "action": "mask",
      "replacement": "[MASKED:credit_card]",
      "category": "credit-card"
    }
  ],
  "immutable": true
}
