docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: The Dashboard page provides a real-time overview of proxy status, traffic statistics, and operational metrics. All widgets auto-refresh every 5 seconds.

docs.title: Summary cards
docs.text: The top of the dashboard displays six summary cards:

docs.title: Proxy status
docs.text: Shows whether the proxy is Running or Stopped, along with the listener count and uptime when running.

docs.title: Active connections
docs.text: Displays the current number of active connections against the configured maximum (e.g., "12 / 1000 max").

docs.title: Total flows
docs.text: Shows the total count of captured flows across all protocols.

docs.title: Intercept queue
docs.text: Displays the number of requests pending in the intercept queue. The count highlights in yellow when items are waiting.

docs.title: Running fuzz jobs
docs.text: Shows the number of currently active fuzz campaigns. The count highlights in blue when jobs are running.

docs.title: Database size
docs.text: Displays the current size of the flow database (formatted as B, KB, MB, or GB).

docs.title: Listeners
docs.text:
When the proxy is running, the Listeners section shows each active listener with:

  • Listener name and listen address
  • Active connection count
  • Uptime

docs.title: TCP forwards
docs.text: If TCP port forwarding rules are configured, this section displays each mapping as a visual arrow from the local port to the upstream target (e.g., :3306 -> db.internal:3306).

docs.title: Flows by protocol
docs.text:
A horizontal bar chart breaks down captured flows by protocol. Each protocol gets a color-coded bar with a count:

  • HTTP/1.x -- Default (gray)
  • HTTPS -- Green
  • WebSocket -- Blue
  • HTTP/2 -- Blue
  • gRPC -- Yellow
  • TCP -- Red

Only protocols with at least one captured flow are shown.

docs.title: Technologies
docs.text:
The Technologies widget displays detected web technologies grouped by host. When multiple hosts are detected, a filter input lets you search by hostname. Each host entry is an expandable accordion showing:

  • Technology name and optional version
  • Category -- Server, Framework, Language, CMS, CDN, WAF, JS Framework
  • Confidence level -- High, Medium, or Low (color-coded badge)

Technologies are grouped by category within each host for easy scanning.

docs.title: Diagnostic budget
docs.text:
The Budget widget shows diagnostic budget usage when budget limits are configured:

  • Request usage -- Progress bar showing requests used vs. maximum allowed, with color changes at 80% (warning) and 95% (danger)
  • Duration limit -- Maximum session duration if configured
  • Stop reason -- Displayed when the proxy has been stopped due to budget exhaustion

When no budget limits are set, the widget shows "No limit".

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
The Rate Limit widget displays the effective rate limiting configuration:

  • Global RPS -- Maximum requests per second across all targets
  • Per-Host RPS -- Maximum requests per second to any single host

When no rate limits are configured, the widget shows "No limit".

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The Configuration section at the bottom summarizes key proxy settings:

Setting Description Listen address Address the proxy is listening on Upstream proxy Upstream proxy URL or "Direct" Max connections Maximum concurrent connections Peek timeout Protocol detection timeout (ms) Request timeout HTTP request timeout (ms) CA initialized Whether the TLS CA certificate is ready

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:
• Settings -- Configure proxy settings
  • Security -- Manage rate limits and budgets

docs.title: Flows
docs.text: The Flows page is the primary interface for browsing captured network traffic. It displays all HTTP/1.x, HTTPS, WebSocket, HTTP/2, gRPC, and TCP flows in a paginated, filterable table.

docs.title: Flow list
docs.text:
The main table shows one row per captured flow with the following columns:

Column Description ID First 8 characters of the flow's unique identifier Protocol Color-coded badge (HTTP/1.x, HTTPS, WebSocket, HTTP/2, gRPC, TCP, SOCKS5+HTTPS, SOCKS5+HTTP) State active, complete, or error Method HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.) or blank for non-HTTP protocols URL Full request URL Status HTTP response status code, color-coded by class (2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx) Messages Message count (relevant for WebSocket and TCP flows) Duration Request-response round-trip time Time Timestamp when the flow was captured

Click any row to navigate to the flow detail view.

docs.title: Filtering
docs.text:
Click the Filters button in the toolbar to reveal the filter panel. You can filter by:

  • Protocol -- Radio buttons for HTTP/1.x, HTTPS, WebSocket, HTTP/2, gRPC, TCP, SOCKS5+HTTPS, SOCKS5+HTTP, or All
  • Method -- Dropdown for GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS
  • Status -- Dropdown for specific status codes (200, 301, 400, 500)
  • Flow state -- Dropdown for active, complete, or error
  • Scheme -- Dropdown for https, http, wss, ws, tcp
  • Host -- Text input to filter by target hostname (debounced)
  • Blocked by -- Dropdown for target_scope, intercept_drop, intercept_cancelled, rate_limit, safety_filter, budget, capacity
  • URL pattern -- Text input with debounced search (300ms delay)
  • Body contains -- Text search within response bodies
  • Tag -- Filter by flow tag

The query API also supports technology and conn_id filters, which can be used via the MCP query tool.

Filters are applied in combination. When any filter changes -- dropdowns and radio buttons as well as text inputs -- the pagination resets to page 1 and the selection is cleared.

docs.title: Auto-refresh
docs.text:
The flow list supports configurable auto-refresh polling. Use the Auto dropdown in the toolbar to set the polling interval:

  • Off (manual refresh only)
  • 1s, 2s, 5s, or 10s

The default polling interval is 2 seconds. You can also click Refresh to manually reload the list.

docs.title: Sorting
docs.text: Click the Duration or Time column headers to sort the flow list by that field. Click again to clear the sort. A downward arrow indicator appears next to the active sort column.

docs.title: Selecting flows
docs.text:
Each row has a checkbox for multi-select. Use the header checkbox to toggle select-all for the current page. When flows are selected, a bulk actions bar appears with the following options:

  • Export HAR -- Export selected flows as a HAR file
  • Delete -- Delete selected flows (with confirmation dialog)
  • Clear -- Clear the selection

docs.title: Flow detail view
docs.text:
Clicking a flow row navigates to the detail page (/flows/{id}), which shows the full request and response data. The detail view includes:

  • Request headers -- Displayed in a key-value table
  • Request body -- With syntax-highlighted viewer
  • Response headers -- Displayed in a key-value table
  • Response body -- With content-type-aware rendering
  • Connection info -- TLS version, server address, timing data

For HTTP/2 and gRPC flows, the detail view shows pseudo-headers (:method, :path, :authority, :scheme, :status) in a separate HTTP/2 info section, and the regular headers table lists only non-pseudo headers. When a message carries only pseudo-headers, the regular headers table is empty rather than repeating them.

When a request or message body was truncated (at capture time, or by the body_max_bytes cap on the query), the body viewer shows a truncation notice instead of presenting the partial body as complete.

A flow blocked with blocked_by: "intercept_cancelled" shows an explanation that the request was held by an intercept rule and the connection or proxy went away before it was released or dropped.

docs.title: Raw tab
docs.text:
When raw bytes are available for a flow, a Raw tab appears alongside the Headers and Body tabs. The Raw tab provides a hex dump view and a text view of the wire-observed bytes, giving you visibility into the exact data as captured on the network.

  • Toggle between Hex and Text display modes
  • Hex mode shows a standard hex dump with offset, hex values, and ASCII representation

Size safeguards

The raw bytes editor shows a warning when the payload exceeds 64 KB. The hex editor is disabled entirely when the payload exceeds 1 MB -- use Text mode for large payloads.

docs.title: WebSocket message list
docs.text:
For WebSocket flows, an enhanced message list replaces the standard message table. Each frame row displays:

  • Sequence number -- #1, #2, etc.
  • Direction arrow -- green upward arrow for send (client-to-server), blue downward arrow for receive (server-to-client)

  • Opcode badge -- color-coded by frame type:

    Opcode Badge color Text Green (success) Binary Blue (info) Close Red (danger) Ping Yellow (warning) Pong Yellow (warning)

  • Size -- human-readable byte size

  • Timestamp -- time with millisecond precision
  • Content preview -- truncated payload preview

Click a message row to expand its detail panel, which provides:

  • Binary messages -- Toggle between Hex dump and Base64 display modes
  • Text messages -- Automatic JSON detection with Pretty / Raw toggle for JSON payloads
  • Close frames -- Parsed status code with description (e.g., 1000 Normal Closure) and close reason text
  • Metadata -- All frame metadata (opcode, masked, fin, etc.) displayed as key-value pairs

docs.title: Export options
docs.text:
From the detail view, you can:

  • Copy as cURL -- Generate a cURL command that reproduces the request
  • Export HAR -- Download the flow as a single-entry HAR file

Both exports drop HTTP/2 pseudo-headers (:method, :path, :authority, :scheme, :status, matched case-insensitively) from the header list. The method, URL, and status come from the flow's top-level fields instead, and HAR entries for HTTP/2 flows report httpVersion: "h2". - Resend -- Navigate to the Resender page with the flow pre-loaded

docs.title: Exporting flows
docs.text:
The toolbar provides two export options:

  • Export JSONL -- Exports all flows (server-side) as JSONL via the manage tool with export_flows action
  • Export HAR -- Downloads selected flows (or all visible flows if none selected) as a HAR file directly in the browser

docs.title: Importing flows
docs.text:
Click Import to open the import dialog. You can import flows from a JSONL file stored in the server's export directory:

  1. Enter the file path relative to the server's export directory (e.g., flows.jsonl). The export directory is set at server start with -export-dir / YP_EXPORT_DIR (default ~/.yorishiro-proxy/exports/); paths that resolve outside it are rejected
  2. Choose a conflict policy:
    • Skip -- Keep existing flows when IDs conflict
    • Replace -- Overwrite existing flows
  3. Click Import

The dialog displays import results including counts of imported, skipped, and errored entries.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
Below the table, pagination controls let you:

  • Navigate between pages with Prev / Next buttons
  • See the current page position (e.g., "1 / 5")
  • Change the number of rows per page (25, 50, or 100)
  • See the total flow count and current range

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:
• Concepts: Flows -- Understanding the flow data model
  • Flow export & import -- Detailed export/import documentation
  • query tool -- MCP tool used by this page

docs.title: Fuzzer
docs.text: The Fuzzer page lets you create, manage, and monitor fuzz testing campaigns. You can define payload positions, configure payload sets, control execution parameters, and analyze results -- all from the Web UI.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text:
The page has two tabs:

  • Jobs -- List of all fuzz campaigns with status and controls
  • New Campaign -- Form for creating a new fuzz campaign

docs.title: Jobs list
docs.text:
The Jobs tab displays a paginated table of all fuzz campaigns:

Column Description ID First 8 characters of the fuzz job ID Flow First 8 characters of the base flow ID Status Color-coded badge: running (blue), completed (green), paused (yellow), cancelled/error (red) Progress Visual progress bar with percentage and count (e.g., "150/500 (30%)") Errors Error count, highlighted in red when non-zero Tag Optional campaign tag Created Creation timestamp Actions Control buttons based on current status

docs.title: Job actions
docs.text:
The available actions depend on the job's status:

Status Available actions Running Pause, Cancel Paused Resume, Cancel Completed (none) Cancelled (none) Error (none)

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text:
The toolbar provides:

  • Status filter -- Dropdown to filter by job status (running, completed, paused, cancelled, error)
  • Tag filter -- Text input to filter by tag
  • Refresh -- Manual refresh button
  • Auto-refresh -- Polling interval selector (Off, 1s, 2s, 5s). Default is 2 seconds.

Click any job row to navigate to the results page for that campaign.

docs.title: Creating a campaign
docs.text: The New Campaign tab provides a comprehensive form for configuring a fuzz campaign.

docs.title: Base flow
docs.text: Enter the Flow ID of the captured request to use as the base for fuzzing.

docs.title: Campaign settings
docs.text:
• Attack type -- Choose between:
    • Sequential -- Test each position one at a time
    • Parallel -- Test all positions simultaneously
  • Tag -- Optional label for the campaign

docs.title: Payload positions
docs.text:
Define where in the request to inject payloads. Click Add Position to add more. Each position has:

  • ID -- Unique identifier for this position (e.g., pos-1)
  • Location -- Where to inject: Header, Path, Query, Body (Regex), Body (JSON), or Cookie
  • Match pattern -- Pattern to find and replace (e.g., FUZZ)
  • Payload set -- Name of the payload set to use for this position (e.g., set-1)
  • JSON Path -- Only shown when location is "Body (JSON)"; specifies the JSON path (e.g., $.key)

docs.title: Payload sets
docs.text:
Define the payloads to inject at each position. Click Add Payload Set to add more. Each set has:

  • Name -- Unique name referenced by positions (e.g., set-1)
  • Type -- One of:
    • Wordlist (values) -- Enter payloads directly, one per line
    • Range (numeric) -- Specify start, end, and step values for numeric sequences
    • File -- Path to a wordlist file on the server

docs.title: Execution parameters
docs.text:
• Concurrency -- Number of parallel requests (default: 1)
  • Rate limit (RPS) -- Maximum requests per second (blank for unlimited)
  • Delay (ms) -- Delay between requests in milliseconds
  • Timeout (ms) -- Request timeout in milliseconds (default: 30000)

docs.title: Stop conditions
docs.text:
Optional conditions to automatically stop the campaign:

  • Error count -- Stop after this many errors
  • Stop status codes -- Comma-separated status codes that trigger a stop (e.g., 500,503)
  • Latency threshold (ms) -- Stop when response latency exceeds this value

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: When macros are defined, a Hooks section allows attaching pre-send and post-receive hooks to the fuzz campaign.

docs.title: Starting the campaign
docs.text: Click Start Fuzz Campaign to begin. You are automatically switched to the Jobs tab to monitor progress.

docs.title: Results page
docs.text: Click a job row to navigate to the results detail page (/fuzz/{id}).

docs.title: Job stats
docs.text:
The top of the results page shows:

  • Status -- Current job status badge
  • Progress -- Visual progress bar with percentage
  • Errors -- Error count
  • Avg duration -- Average response time across all results
  • Status distribution -- Breakdown of response status codes (e.g., "200: 450, 404: 30, 500: 20")
  • Tag -- Campaign tag if set

Job control buttons (Pause/Resume/Cancel) appear in the header for active jobs.

docs.title: Results table
docs.text:
A filterable, paginated table shows individual fuzz results:

Column Description # Result index number Status Response status code, color-coded Length Response body length Duration Response time Payloads Key-value pairs showing which payload was used at each position Error Error message if the request failed (truncated to 40 characters)

docs.title: Filtering and sorting
docs.text:
• Status code -- Filter by specific status code
  • Body contains -- Search within response bodies
  • Sort -- Sort by status code, duration, or body length

Results auto-refresh every 2 seconds for active jobs and stop polling for completed jobs.

docs.title: Result detail panel
docs.text:
Click a result row to open the detail panel showing:

  • Payloads -- Full payload key-value pairs used for this request
  • Error -- Full error message if applicable
  • Response headers -- Complete response header listing
  • Response body -- Full response body with content-type-aware syntax highlighting

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:
• Fuzzer feature -- Detailed fuzzer documentation
  • fuzz_http, fuzz_ws, fuzz_grpc, fuzz_raw -- typed per-protocol fuzz MCP tools

docs.title: Intercept
docs.text: The Intercept page lets you review, modify, and control intercepted requests, responses, and WebSocket frames that match your intercept rules. It operates as a queue where you can inspect each intercepted item and decide what to do with it.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text:
The page has two tabs:

  • Queue -- Shows intercepted requests, responses, and WebSocket frames waiting for your action
  • Rules -- Displays information about intercept rule configuration

docs.title: Intercept queue
docs.text:
The Queue tab displays a table of all currently intercepted items. The queue polls every second while items are pending and backs off to every 5 seconds while it is empty. Polling pauses entirely while the browser tab is hidden and refreshes immediately when you return to it. Each row shows:

Column Description ID First 8 characters of the intercept entry ID Phase Color-coded badge indicating the intercept phase (see below) Method / Status HTTP method badge (for requests), status code (for responses), or opcode + direction (for WebSocket frames) URL Request path and query string, or upgrade URL for WebSocket frames Host Target hostname extracted from the URL Rules Badges showing which intercept rules matched this item Time Timestamp when the item was intercepted

docs.title: Phase column
docs.text:
Each intercepted item has a phase that determines what kind of data it contains and how you can modify it:

Phase Badge color Description request Blue (info) HTTP request before it is sent to the upstream server response Green (success) HTTP response received from the upstream server, before it is returned to the client websocket_frame Yellow (warning) A WebSocket data frame captured during an active WebSocket relay

The page header shows a badge with the current queue count, highlighted in yellow when items are pending.

When the queue is empty, a message prompts you to configure intercept rules.

docs.title: Working with intercepted items
docs.text: Click a row in the queue to select it. The detail panel opens below the queue table, showing editable fields appropriate to the item's phase.

docs.title: Request phase editing
docs.text:
When the selected item is a request, the detail panel provides inline editing for all request components:

  • Method -- Dropdown to change the HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS)
  • URL -- Text input to modify the full request URL
  • Headers -- Key-value editor where you can:
    • Edit existing header names and values
    • Remove headers with the x button
    • Add new headers with + Add Header
  • Body -- Textarea for editing the request body

docs.title: Response phase editing
docs.text:
When the selected item is a response, the detail panel shows:

  • Status code -- Dropdown to change the HTTP status code
  • URL -- Read-only display of the original request URL
  • Headers -- Key-value editor for response headers (same add/edit/remove controls as request headers)
  • Body -- Textarea for editing the response body

The following parameters are sent when you modify and forward a response:

Parameter Description override_status HTTP status code override override_response_headers Replace existing response headers add_response_headers Add new response headers remove_response_headers Remove response headers by name override_response_body Replace the response body

docs.title: WebSocket frame editing
docs.text:
When the selected item is a websocket_frame, the detail panel shows read-only metadata and an editable payload:

  • Opcode -- Frame opcode badge (e.g., Text, Binary)
  • Direction -- client_to_server or server_to_client
  • Flow ID -- The WebSocket flow this frame belongs to
  • Upgrade URL -- The URL from the original WebSocket upgrade request
  • Sequence -- Frame sequence number within the connection
  • Body -- Textarea for editing the frame payload

To modify a WebSocket frame, edit the body and click Modify & Forward. Only the override_body parameter is used for WebSocket frames.

docs.title: Structured and raw view modes
docs.text:
When raw bytes are available for an intercepted item, a Structured / Raw toggle appears at the top of the detail panel. This controls which view you see and which data is sent when you act on the item.

  • Structured (default) -- Shows the parsed HTTP fields (method, URL, headers, body). Edits are applied at the HTTP (L7) layer.
  • Raw -- Shows the captured wire bytes. Edits are applied at the byte level, bypassing HTTP serialization.

The active view mode determines what happens when you click Modify & Forward:

  • In Structured view, your edits to method, URL, headers, and body are sent as structured L7 modifications.
  • In Raw view, the edited raw bytes are sent as raw_override_base64, replacing the entire payload on the wire.

Release and Drop work the same in both views, except that Release in Raw view forwards the original wire bytes without HTTP library normalization.

docs.title: Raw bytes editor
docs.text:
When you switch to Raw view, the detail panel shows the raw bytes editor with two sub-modes:

  • Hex -- A traditional hex dump editor showing offset, hex values, and ASCII representation. You can edit the hex values directly. Changes are parsed back to bytes when you click away from the editor (on blur).
  • Text -- A plain text editor that interprets the raw bytes as UTF-8 text. Useful for editing HTTP/1.x requests where the content is human-readable.

docs.title: Size limits
docs.text:
The raw bytes editor has performance-related limits:

Threshold Behavior > 64 KB A warning is shown that hex editing may be slow > 1 MB Hex editor is disabled; you must use the Text sub-mode instead

The byte size of the raw payload is shown next to the "Raw Bytes" section title.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: Three action buttons appear in the detail header. While an action is in flight, all three buttons are disabled so a double click can't act on the same item twice; after the action completes, the selection is cleared once the queue has been refetched.

docs.title: Release
docs.text: Forwards the intercepted item as-is, without applying any of your edits. In Structured view, the item passes through the normal protocol pipeline. In Raw view, the original wire bytes are forwarded directly.

docs.title: Modify & forward
docs.text:
Applies your edits and forwards the modified item. The behavior depends on the view mode and phase:

  • Structured view -- Your field-level changes (method, URL, headers, body for requests; status, headers, body for responses; body for WebSocket frames) are applied at the protocol layer. Headers are merged using comma concatenation for duplicate names per RFC 7230.
  • Raw view -- The edited raw bytes replace the entire payload on the wire via raw_override_base64.

docs.title: Drop
docs.text: Discards the intercepted item entirely. For requests, a 502 response is returned to the client. For WebSocket frames, the frame is silently dropped. A warning toast confirms the drop action.

docs.title: Rules tab
docs.text:
The Rules tab provides information about intercept rule management. Intercept rules are configured through the MCP configure tool rather than directly in the Web UI. The tab explains how to use the configure tool to add, remove, enable, or disable intercept rules.

Tip

You can manage intercept rules from the Settings page under the Intercept Rules tab, which provides a visual interface for rule management.

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:
• Intercept feature -- Detailed intercept documentation
  • intercept tool -- MCP tool reference
  • Settings: Intercept rules -- Configure intercept rules via the Settings page

docs.title: Macros
docs.text: The Macros page lets you define, edit, execute, and manage multi-step request sequences. Macros are useful for automating workflows like authentication flows, multi-step API interactions, and session management.

docs.title: Macro list
docs.text:
The main page displays a table of all defined macros:

Column Description Name Macro name (unique identifier) Description Optional description text Steps Number of steps in the macro (badge) Created Creation timestamp Updated Last modified timestamp Actions Run, Edit, Delete buttons

Click any row to navigate to the macro detail/editor page.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• New Macro -- Button in the header to create a new macro (navigates to /macros/new)
  • Run -- Execute the macro immediately
  • Edit -- Navigate to the macro editor
  • Delete -- Delete the macro (with confirmation dialog)

The macro list polls for updates every 5 seconds. Polling pauses while the browser tab is hidden.

docs.title: Macro editor
docs.text:
The detail page (/macros/{name}) provides a full editor with two tabs:

  • Editor -- Define and modify macro steps
  • Run & Results -- Execute the macro and view results

docs.title: Defining steps
docs.text:
Each macro consists of one or more steps. Each step specifies:

  • Step ID -- Unique identifier within the macro
  • Flow ID -- The captured flow to use as the base request
  • Override method -- Optionally change the HTTP method
  • Override URL -- Optionally change the request URL
  • Override headers -- Key-value editor for header overrides
  • Override body -- Optionally replace the request body
  • Error handling -- What to do when a step fails:
    • Abort -- Stop the macro
    • Skip -- Skip the failed step and continue
    • Retry -- Retry the step (configurable retry count, delay, and timeout)

docs.title: Template warnings
docs.text:
When you save a macro, the server statically checks its §var§ templates. A variable is reported when it is defined by neither the initial variables, a preceding step's extraction rule, nor a reserved __ key -- typically a typo such as §sesion_cookie§. The macro is still saved; the warnings are shown as toasts (up to three, followed by an "...and N more template warning(s)" summary).

Ignore the warning if you plan to supply the value at run time. Otherwise fix the name: at run time an unresolved §var§ is sent on the wire literally and the step's status becomes warning.

docs.title: Variable extraction
docs.text:
Each step can define extraction rules to capture values from the response for use in subsequent steps. Each extraction rule specifies:

  • Variable name -- Name to store the extracted value (referenced as §variable_name§ in later steps)
  • From -- Whether to extract from the request or response
  • Source -- Where to find the value:
    • Header -- Extract from a specific header
    • Body (regex) -- Extract using a regular expression with capture group
    • Body (JSON path) -- Extract using a JSON path expression
    • Status code -- Capture the response status code
    • URL -- Capture the request URL
  • Default value -- Fallback value if extraction fails
  • Required -- Whether the macro should fail if extraction fails

docs.title: Guard conditions
docs.text:
Steps can have conditional execution via guard conditions. A guard evaluates the result of a previous step and determines whether the current step should execute. Guard options include:

  • Step -- The step whose result to evaluate
  • Status code -- Match a specific status code
  • Status code range -- Match a range of status codes
  • Header match -- Match header key-value pairs
  • Body match -- Match body content
  • Extracted variable -- Check an extracted variable's value
  • Negate -- Invert the condition

docs.title: Running a macro
docs.text:
From the Run & Results tab, click Run to execute the macro. Results are displayed as a table showing each step's outcome:

  • Step ID and flow ID
  • Response status code
  • Duration
  • Extraction results (variables captured from the response)
  • Error information (if the step failed)

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:
• Macros feature -- Detailed macros documentation
  • macro tool -- MCP tool reference

docs.title: Web UI overview
docs.text: The yorishiro-proxy Web UI provides a browser-based interface for inspecting captured traffic, managing proxy settings, and running security testing tools. It is served automatically when you enable the Streamable HTTP transport.

docs.title: Enabling the Web UI
docs.text:
The Web UI is embedded in the yorishiro-proxy binary and served automatically when the HTTP MCP transport is active. By default, HTTP MCP starts on a random loopback port. To use a fixed address:

yorishiro-proxy server -mcp-http-addr 127.0.0.1:9090

Once started, open the URL shown in the startup log in your browser. The Web UI and the MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint share the same address.

To auto-open the browser on startup:

yorishiro-proxy server -mcp-http-addr 127.0.0.1:9090 -open-browser

docs.title: Token authentication
docs.text:
The HTTP MCP transport uses Bearer token authentication (auto-generated by default). To set a fixed token:

yorishiro-proxy server -mcp-http-addr 127.0.0.1:9090 -mcp-http-token my-secret-token

The browser will prompt you for the token on first visit. The token is stored in the browser's local storage for subsequent visits.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The Web UI is a React single-page application that communicates with the proxy backend through MCP tool calls over Streamable HTTP. Every action you perform in the UI -- querying flows, starting the proxy, modifying intercept rules -- is executed as an MCP tool invocation under the hood. This means the Web UI has the same capabilities as any MCP client.

The architecture looks like this:

Browser (React SPA)
  → Streamable HTTP transport
    → MCP Server
      → MCP Tools (query, configure, resend, fuzz, etc.)

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
The Web UI consists of the following pages:

Page Description Flows Browse and filter captured HTTP, WebSocket, gRPC, and TCP flows Dashboard Proxy status overview, traffic statistics, and live widgets Intercept Review and modify intercepted requests before forwarding Resender Edit and resend captured requests with response comparison Fuzzer Create and manage fuzz testing campaigns Macros Define and execute multi-step request sequences Security Manage target scope, rate limits, budgets, and safety filters Settings Configure proxy listeners, TLS, protocols, and plugins

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:
• Quick setup -- Getting started with the proxy
  • MCP configuration -- Configuring MCP transports
  • Architecture -- System architecture overview

docs.title: Resender
docs.text: The Resender page lets you edit and resend captured requests over HTTP, WebSocket, gRPC, and raw TCP. Each send goes through the matching typed MCP tool (resend_http, resend_ws, resend_grpc, or resend_raw).

docs.title: Loading a flow
docs.text:
To start resending, you need to load a captured flow:

  1. Enter a flow ID in the input field (or navigate from the Flows page via the Resend button)
  2. Click Load (or press Enter)

The editor populates with the flow's request data. The interface adapts based on the flow's protocol -- HTTP flows show an HTTP editor, WebSocket flows show a frame editor, gRPC flows show a gRPC editor, and TCP flows show a TCP editor.

Two page mode tabs sit at the top of the page:

  • Resend -- The editor described on this page
  • Compare -- Response comparison. This view is currently suspended and only shows a placeholder; use the Resend tab and compare responses in the send history instead

docs.title: HTTP mode
docs.text: When you load an HTTP or HTTPS flow, the editor presents a split-panel layout with the request editor on the left and response viewer on the right.

docs.title: Editor modes
docs.text:
Two editor mode tabs let you switch between:

  • Structured -- Form-based editor with separate fields for method, URL, headers, and body
  • Raw -- Full raw HTTP message editor for direct text editing

For HTTP/2 and gRPC flows, the structured editor works normally while the raw editor reconstructs an HTTP/1.1 representation with a notice about the downgrade.

docs.title: Structured editor
docs.text: The structured editor provides:

docs.title: Method and URL
docs.text: A dropdown for the HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS) and a text input for the URL.

docs.title: Tag
docs.text: An optional tag field to label the resent request for later identification.

docs.title: Request tabs
docs.text:
Three tabs organize the request editing:

  • Headers -- Key-value editor for request headers. Add, modify, or remove individual headers.
  • Body -- Textarea for the request body content.
  • Body patches -- Patch editor for applying targeted modifications to the request body without rewriting it entirely. See Body patches.

docs.title: Body patches
docs.text:
Each patch row has a mode selector, and the two modes are mutually exclusive:

Mode Fields Description JSON path + value JSON path (e.g., $.path.to.field), new value (JSON) Replace the value at a JSON path Regex + replace Regex pattern, replace string Replace every regex match in the body

Switching modes clears the row's fields. A row with an empty json_path (or empty regex in regex mode) shows an inline validation error, and the Send button stays disabled until every row is valid.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: When macros are defined, a Hooks section appears. It is currently suspended: the typed resend_http tool doesn't accept hooks yet, so the editor is shown greyed out and its values are not sent. To run a macro around a resend, call the macro tool directly or use fuzz_http hooks.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• Send -- Sends the request via resend_http. Disabled while any body patch is invalid
  • Default dry-run (suspended) -- Disabled checkbox. The typed resend tools have no dry-run mode

docs.title: Raw editor
docs.text:
The raw editor provides:

  • Target address -- host:port field (e.g., example.com:443)
  • TLS -- Checkbox to enable TLS for the connection
  • Tag -- Optional tag field
  • Raw HTTP text -- Full editable HTTP message including request line, headers, and body
  • Send Raw button (the dry-run checkbox is suspended here as well)

docs.title: Response viewer
docs.text:
The right panel displays the response after sending:

  • Status code badge (color-coded by class)
  • Duration in milliseconds
  • Response headers and body with syntax highlighting

When no response is available yet, a placeholder message is shown.

docs.title: WebSocket mode
docs.text:
When you load a WebSocket flow, the editor shows a single-frame editor that sends through resend_ws:

  • Target -- host:port. Optional; recovered from the flow when left blank
  • Scheme -- wss or ws
  • Path -- The upgrade path (e.g., /ws/path)
  • Opcode -- text, binary, ping, pong, or close
  • FIN -- Prefilled from the loaded flow's first client frame (ws_fin metadata), so a fragmented frame (FIN=0) is not silently resent as FIN=1
  • Compressed -- Mark the frame as per-message-deflate (RFC 7692) compressed. Shown for text and binary only
  • Payload -- Frame payload, as text or base64
  • Close code / close reason -- Shown for close frames (code 1000--4999)

docs.title: gRPC mode
docs.text:
When you load a gRPC flow, the editor sends a unary call through resend_grpc:

  • Target -- host:port. Optional; recovered from the flow when left blank
  • Scheme -- https or http
  • Service -- Fully qualified service name (package.Service)
  • Method -- Method name
  • Message body -- Plaintext message body. Proto-schema-aware editing is not available in the WebUI yet

docs.title: TCP mode
docs.text: When you load a TCP flow, the editor switches to TCP mode with a different set of controls.

docs.title: TCP mode tabs
docs.text:
• Resend Raw -- Resend raw bytes with optional patches
  • TCP Replay -- Replay all client messages in sequence

docs.title: TCP controls
docs.text:
• Target address -- host:port for the TCP connection target
  • TLS -- Checkbox to enable TLS
  • Tag -- Optional tag field

docs.title: Resend raw
docs.text:
In Resend Raw mode, two tabs are available:

  • Messages -- Read-only list of original TCP messages showing direction (send/receive), size, and content
  • Raw Patches -- Editor for applying byte-level patches to the raw TCP data before resending

Each raw patch row has a mode selector:

Mode Description Offset + Data (base64) Overwrite bytes at a byte offset with base64-encoded data Find/Replace (base64) Find and replace by base64-encoded bytes Find/Replace (text) Find and replace by plain text

The offset field is validated as you type: it must be a non-negative integer, and an empty, fractional, or negative value shows an inline error and disables Send Raw. Only offset patches are sent to resend_raw (its patches parameter is offset-based); find/replace rows are kept in the editor but not applied.

Action: Send Raw (the dry-run checkbox is suspended).

docs.title: TCP replay
docs.text:
TCP Replay re-sends all client (send) messages in their original sequence to the target address. No patching is applied -- this mode is useful for reproducing the exact original interaction.

Action: Replay All button.

docs.title: Response viewer
docs.text: The TCP response viewer shows the raw response data with byte count and duration.

docs.title: Send history
docs.text:
Below the editor, the Send History list shows resend operations recorded server-side, not just from the current browser session: it is backed by query("flows") filtered to origin: "resend", so the list survives a browser reload and opening the WebUI on a different machine surfaces the same history. Each entry shows:

  • Status code badge (--- when there is no status, e.g. raw TCP)
  • Protocol badge
  • Method (or RAW/REPLAY indicator) and target URL or address
  • Tag (if set)
  • Duration
  • Timestamp

Click an entry to open the corresponding flow on the Flow detail page. The list pages server-side with Prev / Next buttons, so deep histories stay responsive.

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:
• Resender feature -- Detailed resender documentation
  • resend_http, resend_ws, resend_grpc, resend_raw -- typed per-protocol resend MCP tools

docs.title: Security
docs.text: The Security page manages target scope rules, rate limits, diagnostic budgets, and SafetyFilter settings. It provides both read-only views of policy-level configuration and editable agent-level controls.

docs.title: Enforcement mode
docs.text:
At the top of the page, a card displays the enforcement mode for each security layer:

  • Effective mode -- The combined mode that applies to all requests
  • Policy Layer -- Mode derived from policy configuration (enforcing if any rules are defined, open otherwise)
  • Agent Layer -- Mode derived from agent-managed rules

Each mode displays as a badge: enforcing (yellow) or open (default).

docs.title: Target scope
docs.text: Target scope uses a two-layer model to control which hosts the proxy can interact with.

docs.title: Policy Layer
docs.text:
The Policy Layer shows rules defined in the configuration file via --policy-allow and --policy-deny flags. These rules are read-only and marked with an "Immutable" badge.

The layer displays two rule tables:

  • Allow rules -- Hosts/patterns that are permitted
  • Deny rules -- Hosts/patterns that are blocked

Each rule shows the hostname pattern, ports, path prefix, and scheme restrictions.

docs.title: Agent Layer
docs.text: The Agent Layer shows dynamically managed rules that you can add or remove at runtime. Each rule table (Allow and Deny) has an Add button to create new rules.

docs.title: Adding a rule
docs.text:
Click Add to open the rule form. Specify:

  • Hostname -- The target hostname pattern (e.g., *.example.com)
  • Ports -- Optional port restrictions
  • Path prefix -- Optional URL path prefix filter
  • Schemes -- Optional scheme restrictions (http, https)

docs.title: Removing a rule
docs.text: Each rule in the Agent Layer table has a remove button. Click it to delete the rule immediately.

docs.title: URL test tool
docs.text:
The URL Test section lets you check whether a specific URL would be allowed or denied by the current scope rules. Enter a full URL (e.g., https://example.com/api/v1/resource) and click Test.

The result shows:

  • Allowed or Denied -- Color-coded badge (green for allowed, red for denied)
  • Layer -- Which layer made the decision (policy or agent)
  • Reason -- Explanation of why the URL was allowed or denied
  • Tested target -- The parsed URL components (scheme, hostname, port, path)
  • Matched rule -- The specific rule that matched, if any

docs.title: SafetyFilter
docs.text:
The SafetyFilter section displays input and output filter rules defined in the configuration. These rules are read-only and belong to the Policy Layer.

The header shows:

  • Enabled/Disabled badge indicating whether the filter is active
  • Immutable badge when the filter cannot be modified at runtime

Two rule tables are displayed:

The two filters run at different layers and serve different purposes. Each table carries a short description that spells this out:

docs.title: Input filter rules
docs.text:
The Input Filter blocks Send-direction payloads on the live wire before they reach the upstream server. Recommended presets: destructive-sql, destructive-os-command. Each rule shows:

  • Name -- Rule identifier
  • Pattern -- Regex or match pattern
  • Targets -- Where the rule applies (header, body, URL, etc.)
  • Action -- What happens when the rule matches (block, warn)
  • Category -- Rule classification

docs.title: Output filter rules
docs.text:
The Output Filter masks sensitive bytes only when an MCP tool returns a recorded flow to the AI agent. The wire copy delivered to the DB, browser, and next hop is never modified. Recommended presets: credit-card, japan-my-number. Output rules additionally show:

  • Replacement -- The text that replaces matched content in the MCP tool response

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text: The Rate Limits section manages request throughput controls using the two-layer model.

docs.title: Effective limits
docs.text:
Shows the combined limits that currently apply:

  • Global RPS -- Maximum requests per second across all targets
  • Per-Host RPS -- Maximum requests per second to any single host

docs.title: Policy Layer
docs.text: Read-only display of rate limits from the configuration file (marked "Immutable").

docs.title: Agent Layer
docs.text:
Editable rate limits that you can adjust at runtime. Click Edit to modify:

  • Global RPS -- Maximum requests per second; 0 means no limit
  • Per-Host RPS -- Maximum requests per second per host; 0 means no limit

The form prefills the current agent values as-is, so an explicit 0 (unlimited) is shown as 0 rather than an empty field and survives Cancel.

Click Save to apply or Cancel to discard changes.

docs.title: Diagnostic budget
docs.text: The Budget section manages request and time limits for diagnostic sessions.

docs.title: Current usage
docs.text:
Shows real-time usage statistics:

  • Requests -- Current request count with progress bar (when a max is set). The progress bar changes color at 70% (warning) and 90% (danger)
  • Duration limit -- Maximum session duration
  • Stop reason -- Displayed when the proxy was stopped due to budget exhaustion

Usage polls every 5 seconds.

docs.title: Effective limits
docs.text: The combined budget limits currently in effect.

docs.title: Policy Layer
docs.text: Read-only budget limits from the configuration file.

docs.title: Agent Layer
docs.text:
Editable budget overrides. Click Edit to modify:

  • Max total requests -- Maximum number of requests allowed (whole number); 0 means no limit and is prefilled as 0
  • Max duration -- Maximum session duration in Go duration format (e.g., 30m, 1h, 1h30m)

Click Save to apply or Cancel to discard changes.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: The Settings page provides a tabbed interface for configuring all aspects of the proxy. It uses the MCP configure, proxy_start, and proxy_stop tools to apply changes.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text:
The Settings page is organized into 12 tabs:

Tab Description Proxy Listener management Capture Scope Control which traffic is captured TLS Passthrough Bypass MITM for specific hosts TCP Forwards Port forwarding rules gRPC Schemas Register .proto schemas for schema-aware gRPC decode Intercept Rules Request interception rules and intercept queue timeout Auto-Transform Automatic request/response modifications SOCKS5 Auth SOCKS5 authentication credentials TLS Fingerprint TLS fingerprinting settings Client Certificate mTLS client certificate configuration Connection Connection limits, timeouts, and per-listener upstream proxy CA Certificate CA certificate management

docs.title: Proxy
docs.text:
Manage proxy listeners (start/stop). The panel shows currently running listeners with their name, listen address, active connection count, and uptime.

To start a new listener:

  1. Click Start New Listener to reveal the form
  2. Configure the listener:
    • Name -- Optional listener name
    • Listen address -- Address and port to bind (default: 127.0.0.1:8080)
    • Upstream proxy -- Optional upstream proxy, set with the upstream proxy editor
  3. Click Start

To stop a listener, click the Stop button next to it (with confirmation).

Protocol selection removed (USK-870)

The previous "Protocols" checkbox group on this panel was removed alongside the deletion of proxy_start.protocols. The half-implemented protocol allow-list had no use case that wasn't already covered by target_scope (host), intercept_rules (request pattern), tls_passthrough (MITM target), and capture_scope (recording target). Use those knobs to scope what the proxy handles.

docs.title: Upstream proxy editor
docs.text:
Both the Start New Listener form and the Connection tab use the same upstream proxy editor. A radio group switches between two modes:

  • Simple URL -- A single upstream proxy URL (e.g., http://host:port or socks5://host:port)
  • Rotation template -- A URL template that is expanded per resolution, plus a rotation policy:
    • Rotation URL Template -- e.g., http://session-§__nonce§:pass@proxy:8080. §__nonce§ expands to a fresh UUID on each resolution; other §var§ macros are also accepted
    • Rotation Policy -- When to resolve a new URL: Per request, Per connection, Per target host, or Sticky

The editor shows warnings as toasts when you save a URL or template that doesn't start with http://, https://, or socks5://, or a rotation template that contains no §var§ macro (every resolution would then return the same URL). Credentials in the URL are redacted (xxxxx) in the confirmation toast.

See Upstream proxy for rotation semantics.

docs.title: Capture scope
docs.text: Configure rules that determine which traffic is captured and stored. You can add include/exclude patterns to scope the capture to specific hosts, paths, or other criteria.

docs.title: TLS passthrough
docs.text:
Manage hosts that should bypass TLS interception (MITM). Connections to these hosts are forwarded directly without decrypting the traffic. Use this for:

  • Certificate-pinned applications
  • Hosts you don't need to inspect
  • Services that break under MITM

You can add and remove passthrough rules from this tab.

docs.title: TCP forwards
docs.text:
Configure TCP port forwarding rules that map local ports to upstream targets. Each forward rule specifies:

  • Local port -- The port to listen on (1--65535)
  • Upstream host -- The target hostname (e.g., db.example.com)
  • Upstream port -- The target port (1--65535)

  • Protocol -- Protocol hint for L7 parsing:

    Value Description auto Peek-based protocol detection (default) raw No L7 parsing, forward raw bytes http Force HTTP/1.x parsing http2 Force HTTP/2 parsing grpc Force gRPC parsing (over HTTP/2) websocket Force WebSocket frame parsing sse Force Server-Sent Events parsing

  • TLS termination -- Enable TLS MITM checkbox. When checked, the proxy terminates the client-side TLS using the target hostname for certificate generation, then applies L7 parsing to the decrypted traffic.

  • Upstream TLS -- Dial upstream over TLS checkbox. When checked, the proxy connects to the upstream target over TLS, independently of the client-side TLS termination setting.

TCP forwards are listener start-time configuration. Adding a forward calls proxy_start with the updated mapping set, so a confirmation dialog (Apply TCP Forward) appears first: applying it resets the listener's in-session settings (intercept rules, transform rules, capture scope, TLS fingerprint, connection limits) and may interrupt in-flight connections on that listener. To remove a forward, restart the proxy with the desired configuration.

Each configured forward is displayed in the mapping list with:

  • A port badge (e.g., :3306)
  • The upstream target (host:port)
  • A protocol badge -- green for an explicit protocol, gray for auto
  • A TLS badge (yellow) when TLS termination is enabled
  • An Upstream TLS badge (yellow) when the upstream is dialed over TLS

This is useful for forwarding non-HTTP protocols (databases, gRPC services, custom TCP services) through the proxy for inspection.

docs.title: gRPC schemas
docs.text:
Register .proto schemas that drive schema-aware decode in query (body_decoded_encoding: "proto-json") and accept body_encoding: "proto-json" on resend_grpc. The card lists the registered schemas and provides:

  • Upload .desc -- Upload a FileDescriptorSet (.desc) file, with an optional source label
  • Discover -- Probe a target's gRPC server reflection service (target address, scheme, optional metadata rows and timeout)
  • Clear all -- Remove every registered schema

Schemaless fallback applies when no schema matches a flow. See the grpc_schema tool.

docs.title: Intercept rules
docs.text:
Manage rules that determine which requests are intercepted and held for review. You can:

  • Add new intercept rules
  • Enable or disable existing rules
  • Remove rules

Intercepted requests appear in the Intercept page queue.

docs.title: Intercept queue
docs.text:
The Intercept Queue card on the same tab configures what happens to items that wait in the queue too long:

  • Timeout (ms) -- How long an item is held before the timeout behavior applies
  • Timeout behavior -- Auto Release (forward unchanged) or Auto Drop

The form is prefilled from the running configuration (query with resource: "config"), so it shows the current values rather than defaults.

docs.title: Auto-transform
docs.text: Configure automatic request and response transformation rules. Auto-transform rules modify traffic in-flight without manual intervention. Each rule specifies match conditions and transformations to apply.

docs.title: SOCKS5 auth
docs.text: Configure SOCKS5 proxy authentication credentials. When the proxy operates as a SOCKS5 server, you can set username/password requirements for connecting clients.

docs.title: TLS fingerprint
docs.text:
View and configure TLS fingerprinting settings. TLS fingerprinting uses uTLS to make the proxy's upstream TLS ClientHello mimic a browser, helping avoid JA3/JA4-based detection by WAFs or bot protection systems.

The available profiles are None (Default Go TLS), Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge, and Random. The proxy defaults to firefox; choose None to use the standard Go TLS stack. See TLS configuration for details.

docs.title: Client certificate
docs.text:
Configure mTLS client certificates for connections to upstream servers that require mutual TLS authentication. You can set:

  • Client certificate file path
  • Client private key file path

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
The Connection tab has two cards.

Connection & Timeouts -- Edit and Save the connection limits:

  • Max connections -- Maximum concurrent connection limit (must be positive)
  • Peek timeout (ms) -- Protocol detection timeout (at least 100 ms)
  • Request timeout (ms) -- HTTP request timeout (at least 100 ms)

Upstream Proxy -- Route outgoing traffic through an upstream HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy, per listener:

  • Listener (scope) -- Select default or any running listener. The editor below is prefilled from that listener's current setting: its rotation template if one is set, otherwise its literal upstream proxy, otherwise the global default
  • The upstream proxy editor -- Simple URL or rotation template. Leave the URL empty to disable the upstream proxy

Click Save to apply the value to the selected listener through configure.

Note

The intercept queue timeout settings moved to the Intercept rules tab.

docs.title: CA certificate
docs.text:
Manage the proxy's Certificate Authority used for TLS interception:

  • View certificate details -- Subject, issuer, validity dates, and serial number
  • Download CA certificate -- Download the root CA certificate in PEM format for installation in your operating system or browser trust store
  • Installation instructions -- Platform-specific guides for macOS, Windows, Linux, Firefox, and Android
  • Regenerate CA -- Generate a new CA certificate (requires reinstallation in trust stores)

Warning

Regenerating the CA certificate invalidates all previously installed certificates. You will need to reinstall the new CA certificate on all devices.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text: Plugin management is no longer in Settings. The read-only Plugins view is at the /plugins route. Plugins load once at proxy boot from config.plugins; to change the loaded set, edit the config and restart the proxy.
